commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(photos): a refused converted photo holds its edits in the photo's own atlas, and the ones born later

edit must not leave: the server still holds the photo inline. assentar knew

now an issue at birth in the dispatcher (recusaDeFotoConvertidaCitada); and

marking, now an issue read from disk (recusasDeFotoConvertida). An ATTACHED
photo's refusal still lets its operations leave with the reference.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(boot): a map booted in a hidden tab waits for the tab instead of mounting over an unloaded style

MapLibre applies a new style on the next animation frame, even one embedded in
the bundle, and a hidden tab gets no animation frames. A page reloaded in the
background (a Vite reload counts) had index.js give up on the map's `load`
after 15 s, and switchLayer then waited 10 s of wall clock for a style that
could not arrive. The boot went on anyway: setupMapFeatures and
reapplyAtlasAppearance threw "Style is not done loading.", the loading screen
dropped over an empty map, and the application's layers only came back on the
next map switch.

`baselayers/style-ready.js` waits for MapLibre's own "done loading" flag with
a timeout that counts only visible time. switchLayer waits for the style on
the map before deciding whether to call setStyle, and again before returning.

Repro: tests/e2e-ui/boot-em-aba-oculta.spec.js emulates a hidden tab (hidden
visibilityState, animation frames held until shown). It fails on the old code
and passed 3 of 3 runs with the fix. tests/unit/style-ready.test.js covers the
visible-time rule and reads the MapLibre contract from the installed library.

fix(sync): a chained whole-bag write no longer erases a colleague's attribute key

Residual loss, pre-existing, found in review of the per-key attributes fix.
A dependent edit (baseOperationId) adopts the revision its predecessor
committed (resolveObservedBase: max(declared base, predecessor version)),
and that revision already holds what a colleague wrote between the declared
base and the predecessor. For a unit the author writes, that is the usual
rule. For the WHOLE attribute bag (the old wire shape, still in persisted
queues), which replaces keys the author never saw, it was a silent loss:

written at 6 is not later than 7, and the replacement drops "z".

The whole bag now reads its keys against the DECLARED base, excluding the
version the immediate predecessor committed (the author's own key).
resolveObservedBase reports predecessorVersion alongside base; its other
caller ignores it. A key written by an earlier link of a longer chain is
still read as a dispute (the receipt names only the immediate predecessor),
which fails closed into a reviewable conflict. Every other path, and the
whole bag's own entry, keep the chained base.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(move): dragging a feature selected before a peer's edit no longer gives that edit back

A drag writes the WHOLE feature, and it wrote it from the copy the selection
took when the feature was selected, which a peer's op does not reach. Two
paths, one cause:

- dragging the feature (move_handler.js -> updateFeatureForMove, for every
  tool; for a symbol with a route, reanchorOnMove translated the copy's route):
  the keypoint a colleague removed came back, and so did the name he changed;
- dragging the route's anchor handle (the anchor branch of _persist in
  trajectory-edit-control.js, which wrote the editor's object whole through the
  owning control): the removed keypoint came back.

The op left on an up-to-date base, so the server accepted it and the peer got
the old value back. Same class as 9ada8c04 and efe9da35, on the two paths
they left out.

Fix:
- move_handler._endDrag rereads the stored features before computing the move
  (rebaseOnStored, new pure helper in pending-edit.helpers.js: properties from
  the stored feature; geometry and runtime `_` keys from the shown copy, since
  _temporalHome decides whether the drag re-anchors). It claims the drag before
  that first await, and the offsets travel with the call, so a second
  mouse/touch end or a new drag cannot interleave. The window left is the one
  between the reread and the document lock of the write.
- the anchor branch now writes through updateFeature({ transform }) under the
  document lock: the stored feature gets the gesture's route diff (as the
  non-anchor branch already did), the new home and the control's
  ensureFeatureConsistency. The shared feature is then rebased in place on what
  was written, and the source is repainted.

Proof: tests/e2e-ui/trajetoria-arrasto-copia-velha.repro.spec.js, two
browsers. A selects a symbol with a 3-keypoint route, B removes the third
keypoint in B's panel, and A drags (1) the symbol body and (2) the anchor
handle. (3) A selects, B renames, A drags. Before: 3/3/3 keypoints on author,
server and peer in (1) and (2), and the old name in (3). After: the peer's
route translated whole in (1), only the departure moved in (2), and the peer's
name kept in (3), with author, server and peer equal.
Chromium 3/3, Firefox 3/3 (--retries=0).
Negative controls: with the move computed over the selection copy, (1) and (3)
fail and (2) passes. With the anchor branch back to updateFeatures(..., true),
(2) fails.

commits.message:
perf(sync): a run of remote updates or deletes on one map is one write of the map document

Measured at scale on 2026-09-24 (two browsers, Postgres, 1000 points; hunt/b61 before
this commit): mass restyle of 1000 took 134 s to reach the server and cost the peer 60 s
of long tasks; undoing it 126 s and 53 s; redoing a delete of 1000, 50 s and 35 s. The

author repair or deferred echo of them, was a read and a write of the whole map document.

writeRunToDocument (create/update) and deleteRunFromDocument (delete, every bucket
searched) keep the single path's rules: an echoed create replaces, an update or delete of
an absent feature is a no-op, the derived analysis output follows its input, and each op
gets its own FEATURE_CREATED / FEATURE_MODIFIED (with previousFeature) / FEATURE_DELETED,
version record (a delete clears the clobber evidence) and REMOTE_OPERATION_APPLIED; the
document is written only when something changed.

absent one -> 1 read, 1 write, 25 FEATURE_MODIFIED with the previous feature, 26 applied;
25 deletes (one of them a line of sight) plus an absent one -> 1 write, points and los
empty, derived halves gone, 25 FEATURE_DELETED. Negative control: with the run limited
to creates both cases fail.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(briefing): a slide edit after the first ack reaches the server

A slide that came back from the server (the echo of the author's own op,
applied as localRepair, and the snapshot) was stored with every server
column next to the client's field: base_layer beside baseLayer,
temporal_enabled beside temporalEnabled, map_id (a UUID) beside mapId (a
name), model_id, photo_id, temporal_cursor, briefing_id, _mapName. The
editor only writes the camelCase field, so the snake_case one went stale,
and the next edit logged the whole slide with both. normalizeSlidePayload
fills a column from its camelCase twin only when the column is absent, so
the server wrote the STALE value: after the first acknowledgement, or
after any F5, changing a slide's base layer, timeline switch, instant,
map, 3D model or 360 photo stayed on the author's screen and never reached
the server, the colleague or the author's own next F5.

- store/sync/slide-shape.js (leaf, zero imports) owns the alias list and
  clientSlideShape, which lived private in the remote handler;
- writeBriefing sends and stores every slide in the client shape, and
  compares against the shaped prior, so shedding the columns alone logs
  no op;
- the SLIDE branch of the handler shapes the localRepair payload too, and
  the snapshot shapes its slides, so the editor stops repainting the form
  on every receipt over a key that exists on one side only (with only the
  write half, that repaint re-armed the autosave right after a save and
  the Back button asked about unsaved changes).

half, 4 red before), tests/integration/slide-colunas-do-servidor-na-
entrada.repro.test.js (entry half; each entry red with its line

fix(sync): two parts of a split batch never leave in the same push

Review finding 2 on ec7de7fc, proven here in two halves.

1. The reservation window. reserveGestureBatchSlots moves the gesture's position at the
   reservation, in the factory, BEFORE enqueueAll; openGestureBatchId then named the
   next part, so a peek in between treated the previous part as complete and sent it
   WITHOUT the tail the transaction was about to write.
   Repro: inside a gesture, 190 ops enqueued, then createBatchOperations for 20 more
   (reserved, not enqueued) -> peek returned the 190 (red). Fix: isOpenGestureBatch holds
   the part being written AND every part the last reservation touched (the transactions
   of a gesture run one after the other, so the next reservation happens only after the
   previous one was enqueued). The queue uses it in the loader and in the census.

2. Packing. The server applies each batchId on its own, so a later part packed into the
   same push behind the tail of the previous one was applied even with that tail refused.
   Repro: batch A (5) and batch B (5) whose ops depend on A's last op -> peek(25) returned
   A+B (red). Fix: the loader stops packing a run that depends on an op already in the
   push. The author's EDIT chain (the dependency that is the op's own baseOperationId)
   keeps sharing the push: the server refuses an edit whose base was not applied, and two
   existing cases (operation-dispatcher, feature-patch-intent) pin that behaviour.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
perf(sync): the author's deferred echoes are replayed together, and a fallback applies one op

Measured on 2026-09-24 in Chromium (author importing 1000 points into a server atlas,
map-document reads counted by call site): 36 to 73 s to reach the server, with 753 reads
of the WHOLE map document in applyRemoteFeatureOpLocked and 211 render refreshes.

Two causes, both in remote-operation-handler.js:
- The broadcast of a push comes back over the socket before the HTTP receipt, while each
  feature is still marked pending, so the author's own echo is deferred and replayed at
  the receipt, one entity at a time (a document read and write each).
- applyRemoteOperations, when a run fell back (its first member pending), applied the
  WHOLE remainder of the run through the single path. With waitForDeferred the first
  member waits for its receipt, after which the rest is clear, but it was already
  condemned to one write per op.

Fix: resolveLocalEdits replays the deferred ops of all resolved entities together, in
server order, through applyRemoteOperations (replayDeferredTogether; if the batch stops,
each entity falls back to its own replayDeferred, and re-applying is idempotent); and a
fallback applies ONE op through the single path and measures the run again from the next.

After: the same import reaches the server in 12.3 s, with 5 single-path reads and 10
render refreshes.

Tests (tests/integration/rajada-remota-um-documento.repro.test.js): 40 deferred echoes
replayed in one write; a frame whose first member is pending (waitForDeferred) writes 2
documents instead of 25. Negative controls: each case fails with its half reverted.

commits.message:
fix(attribute-table): an open cell survives the redraw, so a colleague's edit or a Tab no longer closes it

The table redraws WHOLE on every LAYERS_CHANGED and on every FEATURE_UPDATED of one of its features,
and the redraw replaced the open cell with the rest. Two ordinary paths hit it while someone typed:

- every remote feature op emits LAYERS_CHANGED (store/sync/remote-operation-handler.js), so a
  colleague editing ANY feature closed the cell. Chromium SAVED the half-typed value to the server

  dropped the cell and what was typed, in silence;

  the redraw closed the cell the Tab had just opened. In both browsers, for Nome to Descricao and
  between attribute columns.

The controller now holds every refresh and redraw while a cell is open (`_holdWhileEditing`, asking
the renderer's `hasOpenEdit`) and runs the held one when the cell closes (`onEditClosed`), in a
microtask so a Tab has already opened the next cell (which keeps it waiting), and after the save of
the committed cell, so the reload does not paint the old value back for a moment.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(csv): a GMS seconds mark no longer swallows the next column of the row

A CSV of "Lat/Long (GMS)" coordinates, the format the import panel offers,
imported ZERO points through the Importar tab. csv-parser.js opened a quoted
section on ANY double quote of an unquoted field, in three places (_parseLine,
_splitLines, detectSeparator). RFC 4180 opens quoting only at the start of a
field; mid-field the quote is a literal. In 22°57'6.898"S;43°12'37.753"W the
text between the two seconds marks, separator included, became one field:
every row lost a column, every coordinate was invalid. With ONE mark per line
the line splitter also stayed "inside quotes" across the newline and glued the
rows. The converter's unit tests use exactly that notation but feed rows to
convertRowToLatLng directly, never through the parser.

Now a quote opens quoting only when the field so far is empty or whitespace, in
the line splitter (which receives the separator, or the three candidates while
detecting it) and in the field parser; detectSeparator counts fields with the
same parser. A field that starts with a quote is still RFC 4180 (commas,
newlines and doubled quotes inside), asserted as a control.

Proof: csv-aspas-no-meio-do-campo.repro.test.js (node, 4 cases) and
cobertura-importar-csv-coordenadas.spec.js, a new coverage spec that imports

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(sync): every gesture above LOTE_MAX_OPS travels in chained parts, composites included

Owner decision B6.1, widened on 2026-09-24: no gesture the interface offers may fail to
reach the server because it has too many operations. b3d22b33 split only the same verb
over independent features; transferring a layer, grouping and undo/redo of composites
above 200 were still refused whole.

Rule: any logical batch above MAX_OPS_PER_LOGICAL_BATCH (a transaction, or an ambient
gesture) travels in parts of up to 200 in batchIndex order (contiguous), each its own
batchId, and the FIRST op of each part carries dependsOn = [last op of the previous
part] (createBatchOperations; in gestures reserveGestureBatchSlots hands out idAt and
link). The queue already refuses to hand over an op whose dependency has a problem
(PendingBlockade) and the flush pushes one part at a time with the receipt before the
next, so a part leaves only after the previous one was applied and a refused part
HOLDS the following ones: a group_feature never reaches the server ahead of the group
(it would write zero rows and be acked as a success). The dispatcher's edit chaining now
ADDS to dependsOn instead of replacing it. describeRefusedPart names the part, how many
changes arrived (the first index of the refused part) and how many stay pending (the
parts reachable through dependsOn). The server ignores dependsOn; no server change. The
splittable flag and the same-verb predicates of b3d22b33 are gone (every gesture splits).

Author throughput (measured while scaling): the receipts of one push are now resolved
together (resolveLocalEdits: repairs through applyRemoteOperations), and the create run
accepts the author's own echo and a run of moves sharing one origin map.

Proof:
- tests/e2e/lote-partido-parte-recusada.e2e.test.js (real server): import of 450 with the
  map locked before push 2 -> pushes [200, 200], part 3 never sent, 200 on the server,
  250 problems, notice "parte 2 de 3 ... 200 de 450 alteracoes ja chegaram; as outras 250";

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(sync): a server copy made right after placing a picture no longer comes out without it, silently

The feature of an image is born PREPARED and the outbound dispatcher holds it until
its bytes are confirmed; the two copies the server makes (clone the atlas, and
"Duplicar" of a map in a server atlas) copy what the SERVER has. Neither door knew
about this computer's pending work: "Copiar no servidor" on atlas.html read no
queue at all, and the map door flushed, which does not release an operation held
behind its bytes. Measured: 1 clone in 3 in the first run of
imagem-copias-leva-bytes; on a slow link the window is tens of seconds.

- atlas.html: before cloning, pendenciasDoAtlasNesteComputador counts, for that
  atlas, the queued operations (held ones included) and the unconfirmed picture
  uploads, reading by getStoreFor without mounting, and only for an atlas this
  computer registered (an atlas never opened here owes nothing and its databases
  are not created by the read). Non-zero, or unreadable, asks first: "Há alterações
  deste computador ainda não enviadas neste atlas / A cópia não as terá. Abra o
  atlas para que elas sejam enviadas e copie depois.", with "Copiar mesmo assim".
- Map "Duplicar": after the flush, esperarEnvioDoMapa waits up to 8 s for the map's
  debt (its operations and its pictures' pending bytes) to reach zero, flushing as
  it goes and saying why ("Enviando as alterações deste mapa antes de duplicar.");
  it asks at once when only refused work is left, and asks the same way when the
  time runs out. Declining returns `cancelled`, which the maps tab does not toast.

fix(attribute-table): whoever cannot edit reads the table, and a lock arriving closes the cell out loud

The attribute-table button lives on the layer row, and the CSS that hides the layers tab's edit
commands under `.map-locked` took it along. That class follows `semEdicaoSync()`, which answers for
BOTH axes, so a Leitor, a Comentarista and anyone on a locked map had no table at all, although the
table already had a read-only mode nobody without editing could reach. With the table open, a lock
arriving left the write commands alive: the open cell painted a value nothing saved, "Adicionar
atributo" did nothing, and "Remover atributo" asked for confirmation and removed nothing, all silent.

"Adicionar atributo", no "Remover atributo" menu, no cell editing; CSV, minimize and close stay. The
controller subscribes to `assinarEdicaoIndisponivel`; when editing becomes unavailable it closes the
open cell WITHOUT saving before redrawing and says so ("A edicao da celula nao foi gravada." plus the
lock or level phrase), because the redraw alone commits the cell in Chromium (blur on removal) and
drops it silently in Firefox. The renderer asks again at commit time, and the remove and cell-edit
handlers refuse out loud instead of returning in silence. Unlocking gives the commands back.

fix(sync): a slide copy goes under the briefing it was added to, and a reorder reaches slide_order

Two defects found by the briefing coverage, measured in Postgres from two
real browsers (a probe of the import-slides modal and the drag reorder):

1. Importing slides from briefing X into briefing Y created the copies under
   X on the server. The copied slide carries X's `briefing_id` (a snapshot or
   canonical slide spreads every column, and the copy keeps it), and
   normalizeSlidePayload only used the envelope's parent when the payload had
   none. After an F5 the copies were gone from Y and sat as orphans at the end
   of X. The envelope's parent (op.mapId, which the client always sets to the
   briefing) now wins; the payload's is the fallback for a caller without one.

   client stores the `slide_order` the canonical receipt and the snapshot give
   it, every later envelope sent it back STALE, and normalizeBriefingPayload
   kept a given slide_order over the slides array. A drag reorder never
   reached the column, and an F5 showed the old order. With a slides array the
   order is now derived from it; a payload with only slide_order keeps it.

Proof: slide-pai-e-ordem-do-briefing.repro.test.js (4 cases: envelope parent

splittable when the undo entry is the same verb over distinct features

across parts; a refused part is named (describeRefusedPart). Composite gestures stay
atomic. No server or envelope change.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(kmz): the viewshed comes out of the KMZ with its green and red fill, not a white blot

On the map the output of a viewshed is two filled multipolygons, green
(visible) and red (obstructed), with the opacity chosen in the panel
(`fill-color: ['get', 'color']`, `fill-opacity: ['get', 'opacity']`). The KMZ
exporter classified the `processed_visibility` bucket as a LINE (none of the
lists of kmz-feature-types.js named it, and LINE is the default), so each
half went out with a `<LineStyle>` only, and a KML Polygon without
`<PolyStyle>` is filled with the spec default, opaque white: in Google Earth
the analysed area became a white blot over the terrain. Even as an AREA the
colour would not come: `resolveFill` read `fillColor`, and the half carries

stopPresence resets the throttle; its timer is tracked and cancelled by cleanup().

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(image): one transfer per image id, and a refused save drops the upload instead of sending it

Review of 12abab25 (the image tool no longer waits for the upload), two findings:

1. The durable blob queue had no single-flight per image id. retomarBlobsPendentes re-read every
   PENDENTE record and re-sent it, including one whose FIRST attempt was still on the wire (the
   record is written before the transfer starts). With the tool not waiting, two pictures in a
   row go up in parallel, and a resumption (the 15 s timer after a transient failure, a
   reconnection) added a duplicate stream of the same bytes: on a 5000 B/s link, three streams
   plus the push each fall under the 2000 B/s floor uploadDeadlineMs is sized for, all get cut,
   and the cycle can repeat. And the duplicate's verdict was written from the record read before
   the original ended, so a duplicate failing AFTER the original confirmed put PENDENTE back on
   disk over CONFIRMADO and kept the feature's operations held.
   Now: a set of ids in flight (_emVoo) owned by tentar and by the batch path of enfileirarBlobs;
   the resumption skips an id in flight and RE-READS the record after its backoff wait, skipping
   one another attempt already settled.

2. The tool registered the pendency AND started the transfer before creation.save. A save refused
   in between (the map locked by a colleague) uploaded bytes for a feature that does not exist,
   left the pendency retrying for up to 300 s, and a refusal told the person about a figure that
   was never on the map. Now registrarEnvioDeImagem (image-sync.js) only registers and hands back
   enviar() and descartar(): the tool sends after the save succeeded and drops the record
   (descartarBlobRegistrado) when it refused. The registration still precedes the save, so the
   operation is still born held.

Proof:
- blob-upload-queue.test.js: two concurrent attempts on one id (the first held on the wire, a
  resumption started meanwhile; the first confirms, a duplicate would fail after it): one transfer
  and the record CONFIRMADO; red with the in-flight checks removed (two transfers). Dropping a
  registration releases the hold, leaves no pendency and sends nothing.
- ferramenta-de-imagem-envia-depois-de-gravar.test.js: the tool's order read in the source
  (register, save, discard on a refused save, then send, never awaited); red on the parent.
- Browser, run with no source edit in between: figura-aparece-na-hora-em-link-lento (5 cases),
  subida-de-imagem-pendurada and browser-collab-imagem-retomada, 9 of 9 green; the picture shows
  in 484 ms at 40 kbps.
- Full frontend suite: only teto-de-peso (the complete graph and the import_export count), both red
  on the base with this change reverted; not re-measured here, per the brief.

fix(session): the exit guard spares another tab's atlas, says the time left, and never vetoes on an account switch

marker, which on a page without a map names what ANOTHER tab (the map) has

window, and the exit-failure sentences used the full window over a veto stamped

(minutes); without it the sentence says "tempo limitado", never a number. The
mounted atlas's failure sentence and the map's logout use rescueVetoRemainingMs,
and an expired veto no longer counts as retention.

through an account switch, and the next account opening that atlas inside the
window would push it under its own token. On an account switch
(endPreviousAccountIfReplaced -> trocaDeConta) the cap does not apply, as in the
mounted rescue, and an adoption that fails releases the veto so the sweep that

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(comments): a text edit no longer reopens a thread a colleague resolved, and vice versa

A comment update sent the sender's WHOLE local copy, and two consequences
followed, both measured with two real browsers and the sync POST held to fix
the interleaving:

1. The author edits the text while an Editor resolves the thread. The text
   edit carried the author's copy's status ('open'); the server writes the
   status from any payload that carries one, so the edit REOPENED the thread
   on the server and on every client, and the resolution vanished with no
   message.
2. The Editor resolves with a copy older than the author's latest text. The
   server's moderation gate (commentEditDenialReason) accepts a non-author
   update only if every other field equals the stored row, so the resolution
   was REFUSED ("Somente o autor pode editar o comentário.") because the copy's
   text was stale; and the peer, which replaced its copy with whatever arrived,
   would otherwise have shown the moderator's old text over the author's.

Fix: commentUpdatePayload (store/comment.operations.js) sends only what the
gesture decided. An edit that did not ask for a status carries none (the
server keeps the column); a moderator's status change carries only
{ id, status, updatedAt } (the server never writes a moderator's body). The
local document stays whole. applyRemoteCommentOp MERGES an update over the
local copy instead of replacing it. The pin drag passes only { id, lng, lat }
instead of the overlay's copy of the whole comment. No server change: the
server already keeps the status when the payload has none, and never writes a
moderator's data.

Proof: comentario-edicao-depois-do-par.repro.spec.js, four cases, every gesture
through the UI (Shift+C + map click + compose, the card's edit and resolve
controls). The two concurrent cases were red before (server "open" after the
resolution; the reverse case never reached "resolved") and are green after;
negative control (the three source files reverted) turns both red again. The
two sequential cases (edit after receiving the colleague's) were green before
and after: the stale-base hypothesis for comments is refuted. Unit: a merge
describe in remote-operation-handler.test.js (moderator's status keeps local
text, author's edit keeps local resolution, create stays whole), red with the
handler reverted. comment-draft-collaboration, comment-author-editing and
import-comment-warning green; frontend vitest 879/879.

Found on the way, not a product bug: a comment created through the store with
no authorId (as comment-draft-collaboration's setup does) cannot be resolved by
an Editor, because the server compares the payload's null authorId with the
authoritative column. The real compose always passes the author.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(sync): a collaborator's unsent work survives the atlas going away under them

Two ways a server atlas disappears for a collaborator B who still has work the server
never received, measured with two real browsers against the real backend:

1. The owner sends the atlas to the bin. The server tells the room (atlas_deleted) and
   B's tab tore the atlas down with clearAllDataStore(), which empties data AND queue:
   the point B had drawn and not yet sent was gone, from no atlas anywhere
   (_handleRemoteAtlasDeleted, account/account.control.js). The bin gives the owner back
   the SERVER's atlas, never B's queue.
2. The owner revokes B's share. The collab gateway closes B's socket with 4003 "access
   revoked" (reconcileAuthorization), and the client read it as a network drop: it
   reconnected forever, the badge said "N pendentes / reconectando" 45 s later, new edits
   kept entering the queue, and nothing said they would never be sent. A reload led to
   the list with "Atlas nao encontrado ou sem acesso" and the queue in a namespace no
   screen shows.

Fix:
- ws-client.js emits `accessRevoked` on a close with code 4003 and reason "access
  revoked" (the reconnect is still scheduled). sync-engine.js asks the server once
  (getAtlas); only on 403/404 it disconnects and raises ATLAS_DELETED_REMOTE with
  `motivo: 'sem-acesso'`, so a close the next reconnect would survive stays a reconnect.
- _handleRemoteAtlasDeleted, when the atlas went away under a COLLABORATOR (a peer's
  delete or lost access), counts the queue first; with work (or an unknown count) it
  takes the rescue the session-loss exit already uses (preserveUnsyncedWorkAsLocal)
  instead of the wipe, and the chooser says where the work went. A failed rescue does
  not wipe either (the namespace is retained). The owner's own delete keeps the wipe.
- atlas-drive.js: arrival notices for "excluido-por-outro-resgatado/-sem-resgate" and
  "sem-acesso", "sem-acesso-resgatado/-sem-resgate".

Proof: frontend/tests/e2e-ui/atlas-some-com-trabalho-pendente.repro.spec.js (B's send
is held by aborting its sync route, so the point is queued with the socket alive):
bin -> B lands on the list with "... foi guardado neste computador como um atlas local"
and the point is in a local atlas; revoke -> the same, instead of reconnecting forever;
control: revoked with no pending work -> "Seu acesso a este atlas foi removido." Red
before (3/3; the point found in NO local atlas after the bin), green after 3/3;
negative control (rescue branch and the 4003 emit disabled) red again 3/3.
browser-delete-atlas, browser-collab-permissions, browser-sharing-lifecycle and
browser-atlas-drive green (13). sync-engine.test.js: the wired-handler list gains
accessRevoked, plus a confirmed and an unconfirmed revocation case (101/101).

Not covered: B OFFLINE when the share is revoked (the reconnect upgrade is refused
without a 4003 frame, so the loop still spins until a reload, where the open fails with
"sem acesso" and the queue stays in the retained namespace).

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(maps): "Duplicar" in a server atlas copies on the server, so the copy is not empty after F5

MapManager.copyMap composed the copy on the client: the layers through a raw
repository write (duplicateMapLayers) before the map existed and without any
operation, and the features INSIDE the document handed to addMap, whose map
CREATE the server does not read to create features. Measured with two real
browsers: in Postgres the copy had one default layer and ZERO features (after
F5 the copy was empty), the author's copy had features pointing at a layer
that never existed, and the peer received the feature through the envelope,
equally orphaned. Data loss on a common command.

Fix (coordinator's decision, option a): in a server atlas "Duplicar" calls the
REST duplicate route, one of the declared structural exceptions for an
entity-whole operation, after flushing the queue (what the author still has
for the source is not on the server yet), and the author receives the copy by
the same path as every peer, a snapshot (syncEngine.resync). A local atlas
keeps the local composition. Offline, the command is still offered and the
click is refused naming the state; a request that fails for lack of network
before the socket notices gives the same refusal.

The route now takes an optional body { name } (validated: trimmed, 1..255),
so the copy is born with the name the person typed. Without it the server
names it "<source> (cópia)", and a second duplicate of the same map collides
with the first copy, while the client resolves maps by NAME: a rename after
the fact could hit the wrong map. Additive and optional; the old call with no
body keeps its behaviour.

Proof: duplicar-mapa-no-servidor.repro.spec.js, two real browsers + Postgres +
F5 on both. Before (map.manager reverted): red, 0 features of the copy on the
server, features pointing at a nonexistent layer on both disks; the offline
case finds no refusal. After: 2/2 green WITH the backend of cb922c83 and
5b2c1acb (already in hunt/integra) applied in the working tree. On this branch
alone the feature/server/F5 counts are green but the "feature points at a
layer of the copy" assertions stay red: the server clone copied
properties.layerId verbatim, and those two integrated commits are what realign
it (clone) and serve the layer from the column (snapshot). Backend:
duplicar-mapa-com-nome.test.js (name used and trimmed, no name keeps the
suffix, empty/oversized/non-string refused with 422); atlas clone and duplicate
suites green. Frontend vitest 879/879, duplicate-map contract e2e,

value is the opening one anyway) and keeps the stored value; the others go
back to the snapshot. This person's changes are still discarded, nobody
else's are.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(briefing): a peer's slide text reaches the open editor without the paste path

Review finding on d67636e4 (critical). _refreshSlideForm built the new rich
text with quill.clipboard.convert({ html }), which runs the PASTE matchers.
createPastedImageMatcher took every data: figure out of the delta and queued
it as pasted; a tick later the queue called getSelection(true), stealing the
focus from where the person was typing, recompressed the figure and
reinserted it as a 'user' change at the last cursor, deleting what that
cursor had selected. The text-change saved it, the peer's editor did the same
on receiving it, and the two editors fed each other: the figure moved, the
selected text vanished, and the whole base64 travelled every few seconds.

Fix: replaceQuillContentSilently writes the stored (already sanitized, already
compressed) HTML straight into the root, folds it into Quill's model with
update('silent') (no text-change), clears the history (Quill records even a
silent change, and Ctrl+Z would have undone the peer's edit and saved that),
and carries the caret across the change with Delta.transformPosition when the
editor has the focus.

Also: _renderSlideEditor is called without await (slide click, a peer's change
of a non-text field) and awaits twice before it is done appending; two
overlapping renders both appended their groups and the form ended with two
rich-text editors (seen once as a Playwright strict-mode violation, two
.ql-editor, in a batch run; not reproduced deterministically). A render that
finds itself superseded after an await, or after Quill loads, now stops.

Proof: briefing-editor-figura-do-colega.repro.spec.js, two real browsers: A
pastes text with a figure, leaves a word selected in the rich text and moves
to the title; B appends text. Before (editor at d67636e4): red, focus stolen
to .ql-editor, the selected word deleted, slide version 3 -> 8 on the server
in 8 s with nobody typing. After: green, focus stays in the title, text
intact, one figure, version stable. 26 briefing specs green.

fix(collab): a superseded remote render repaints, and unwire clears its timers

Review 4A finding on b3a92952 (integrated as 5d913a4c): setupMapFeatures reads the

run A reads the features (photo P included) and stalls on the blob; the watchdog opens
the gate; a colleague deletes P; run B draws without P; A settles and P REAPPEARS, and

armed (house rule: every timer is cleared).

the store (or, if a newer one is running, marks it dirty for a trailing one). unwire
cancels the pending timer (new injectable cancelScheduled, default clearTimeout) and
the watchdog of the running refresh.

fix(collab): over the socket a tail above the cap asks for an HTTP resync, never a snapshot frame

Review 4A of 57f0cfcb (integrated as 3cd6b9bb) against f14f143e: the cap
swapped a tail above 500 ops for the snapshot on BOTH doors, whatever the
snapshot's size. The client asks for its tail over the SOCKET on every
reconnect, and the WebSocketServer runs without perMessageDeflate, so on a
slow downlink the snapshot became one uncompressed frame of the whole atlas:
a peer at 40 kbps in a ~5 MB atlas that reconnects while a colleague imports
600 features got a frame of ~1000 s, the escalated heartbeat cuts it at 400 s,
the next sync_request starts from the same cursor and gets the same frame, in
a loop until F5, holding the link the HTTP push needs (the 600-create tail
itself was a few hundred KB).

pullOperations takes `longTail`: 'snapshot' (the default, the REST pull,
unchanged) or 'resync'. handleSyncRequest asks for 'resync', and a tail over
the cap is then answered with no snapshot at all: the socket sends the frame
the client already reads as "re-pull the atlas over HTTP" (`atlas_updated`,
routed to serverResync, which runs resync(): compressed, bounded by silence),
and every held operation frame is dropped, since the snapshot that HTTP pull
brings is read after this point and covers them. No new frame type, no
contract change; the extra `resync: 'cauda-longa'` field is informative only.

socket answers a small atlas_updated and no sync_response; 500 ops: the tail
still comes over the socket). Negative control: without longTail 'resync' the

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(sync): a briefing or slide receipt no longer loses its confirmed revision

BRIEFING and SLIDE are CONVERGENCE_GUARDED, so every receipt runs
confirmEntityVersion (stamps the revision the server committed) and then
resolveLocalEdit, which re-applies the author's own op through the inbound
path. applyRemoteBriefingOp and applyLocalSlideIntent wrote the op's payload
over the stored entry, with the confirmedVersion of BEFORE the edit (or none,
on a create). The author's second consecutive edit of a slide title, a
briefing name, or a second slide appended (which moves the briefing order)
declared a base the server had passed and was refused as disputed fields: a
durable issue that blocks the entity and, by batchId, the whole batch. A
create lost the stamp and the next edit left with no base. On a peer, the
colleague's payload carried the colleague's pre-edit base and it was stored
as this client's confirmed revision, so the peer's next edit was refused.

Same defect inboundSideEntity closed for 3D/360 on 2026-09-22, same rule:
on the author's repair keep the stamp on disk; on a peer's op, no base.
applyRemoteBriefingOp now reads the stored briefing on create too (only the
update merges slides, as before) and receives localRepair; the SLIDE case
passes localRepair to applyLocalSlideIntent, which runs the entry through
inboundSideEntity against the slide it replaces.

Proof (node, real handler, queue and repository on fake IndexedDB, the
receipt order of sync-engine.js): recibo-briefing-slide-base-confirmada
.repro.test.js, four cases from the integration reviewer's repros (slide
create -> receipt -> edit -> receipt -> edit declares 6; a colleague's slide
leaves no base; briefing rename twice declares 3; a colleague's briefing
leaves no base). All four red before. Negative control: slide half reverted
-> cases 1-2 red; briefing half reverted -> cases 3-4 red. Also green:
briefing-slides-concorrentes, browser-collab-briefing-temporal,

commits.message:
fix(sync): the durable cursor also carries the per-atlas level of its recorte

Review of 7b7f0f27 (lot 4A): the server cuts the snapshot by LEVEL too, not only
by principal. A read snapshot has no spatial comment and a read tail filters
them out, so a Leitor promoted to Comentarista kept a generation without the
comments made before the promotion, and every later connect asked only for the
tail from that cursor: those comments never arrived. sharing_updated only
updated the role.

The level is only known once the socket answers (connected, or a live
sharing_updated), after the first pull. _markRecorteLevel stamps the active
generation with it: a generation with no level (a snapshot this connect just
staged) is stamped; one staged under another level gets its cursor zeroed,
which makes both the next connect and the "same version" shortcut of
applyRemoteSnapshot pull and stage in full, and a resync runs now. A snapshot
activation carries the level only when the session already knows it
(SyncSession.nivel), so a fresh snapshot never inherits the previous
generation's level.

record in two integration files now include the stamped level.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(import): valid UTF-8 beats a stale XML header, and one broken byte no longer flips the file

Review of 3cbb9a80 (integrated as f41c0c76) found three regressions of files that were read
RIGHT before it, in texto-de-arquivo.js:
(a) an XML declaring encoding="utf-16" with 8-bit bytes (.NET XmlWriter over a StringWriter)
    was decoded as UTF-16 into CJK garbage;
(b) an XML declaring ISO-8859-1 with valid UTF-8 bytes came out "SÃ£o Paulo";
(c) ONE byte that is not UTF-8 (a truncated file; a DBF field cut mid-character by its fixed
    width) turned the whole file, or the whole DBF via dbfPrecisaDeCpg, into Windows-1252, so
    every correct accent became mojibake where before only that character was lost.

The rule now: BOM; else UTF-8 when the bytes LOOK like UTF-8 (more valid multibyte sequences
than invalid bytes, or pure ASCII: contarSequenciasUtf8 / pareceUtf8); else a single-byte
encoding, the one an XML declaration names when supported and not UTF-16, Windows-1252
otherwise. The same counting decides dbfPrecisaDeCpg. The test that claimed "a declared
ISO-8859-1 is honored even when the bytes would pass as UTF-8" used Latin-1 bytes, which are
not valid UTF-8, so it did not prove what it said: renamed to what it does prove, and the real
case added. Also a stale comment in import.control.js ("reads through file.text()").

Proof: tests/unit/texto-de-arquivo-importado.test.js, four REGRESSION cases and a counting
control. Negative control with the previous texto-de-arquivo.js (the two new exports stubbed):
the four regression cases fail. Browser specs unchanged and green (importar-arquivo-codificacao,

commits.message:
fix(sync): drop the analysis-output writes an older client left refused

Before 2b05ce0c the tools journaled a FEATURE op for every output half
(`<losId>-visible`, `-obstructed`) and the server refused each one. A person
who used the line of sight or the viewshed in an atlas of the server before
the fix keeps those refusals in the durable journal forever ("Recusas: 2"),
and they hold the queue census red with nothing left to decide: the output
is now derived per client, so nothing is lost by dropping them.

Fix: isDerivedOutputOperation (store/analysis-output.js) recognizes such an
op WITHOUT the new `storage` stamp, by type: the id must be a half's id AND
the payload's source must be an analysis input (a non-UUID id of any other
type is not matched and keeps failing loudly).

pending, through the same dequeue a receipt uses (journal metadata and the
durable issue go with the envelope). The sync engine runs it once per
session, in connect and before the first flush, because a queue holding only
refusals is never flushed.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(boot): a refused collab WebSocket no longer tells the person to check a connection that works

Measured with the collab WebSocket upgrade refused and plain HTTP working (a proxy or firewall
that does not pass WebSocket, common on corporate and military networks): the open pipeline
pulls the atlas over HTTP, then waits for the socket's `connected` frame; the handshake promise
rejects, openAtlasFromUrl sends the tab back to atlas.html?aviso=abertura-falhou, and the chooser
said "Nao foi possivel abrir o atlas. Verifique sua conexao e tente de novo." on a page whose
server list had just loaded. Every retry repeats the round trip. The atlas cannot be opened at
all in that network, and the sentence sent the person after the wrong thing.

The rejection of a handshake that closes before `connected` now carries a code
(WS_HANDSHAKE_CLOSED, ws-client.js), the boot maps it to its own arrival notice
(abertura-sem-tempo-real), and the chooser says what the code knows and what the person can do:
"Nao foi possivel abrir o atlas: o servidor respondeu, mas a conexao em tempo real nao abriu.
Tente de novo; se continuar, avise o administrador." True for every way it happens (a proxy, a
firewall, an upgrade refused for the account); no cause is claimed.

Not changed, and reported for a product decision: that a server atlas cannot be opened at all
without the WebSocket, and that the outbound flush requires the socket ONLINE.

Proof, tests/e2e-ui/abertura-sem-tempo-real.repro.spec.js (every collab socket of B closed by the
route; toast read after its computed opacity passes 0.9): before, the old sentence (red); after,
the new one (green). Unit: ws-client.test.js pins the code on the rejection;
seus-atlas-sem-servidor.test.js pins the notice and its session gate.

load in one run (passes alone, 10/10).

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(auth): a republished public link does not revive the old link's visitor tokens

The public-link visitor token (getAtlasByPublicLink, 1 h) carried only the
atlas, and every door that honours it asked only whether the atlas was PUBLIC.
Unpublishing killed it (the atlas stopped being public), but republishing
mints a NEW link: the owner who unpublishes because the link leaked and then
republishes for the right people handed read access back, over REST and the
collaboration socket, to every token issued by the leaked link in the last
hour, without anyone opening the new link. Clause 5.4 of CONSTITUICAO.md says
the link is revocable; this is the case where the revocation did not hold.

The token now carries `pl`, a fingerprint (SHA-256, 16 hex) of the link it
came from (src/utils/public-link-fingerprint.js; a fingerprint and not the
link, which is the secret that mints new tokens). Both mappers surface it as
req.user.publicLinkFp; requireAtlasPermission (every HTTP door, the 3D and 360
asset reads included) treats the atlas as public to a visitor token only when
the fingerprint matches the CURRENT link; the gateway checks it on the
handshake and on reconciliation (ws.publicLinkFp). The 3D asset memo key
includes the fingerprint so an old-link token cannot ride a cached answer. A
visitor token minted before this change has no `pl` and is refused; the
visitor reloads the link (first deployment is a fresh install).

Repro: tests/integration/link-publico-republicado-nao-revive-token.repro.test.js
(REST read and socket handshake with the old link's token after a republish:
red before, refused after; the new link's token reads and connects). Negative
controls: reverting each comparison turns its case red. tests/ws/collab-reauthz
now builds its visitor socket with the fingerprint, as the gateway does. Public
token, permission, tile and asset suites and tests/ws green; frontend e2e
contract 70/261 green.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(sync): a hung image upload no longer holds the picture and every later edit forever

The image bytes travel by POST /images/bulk (bulkUploadImages), which had no deadline at all,
and the image tool awaits the upload BEFORE it writes the feature. A request that never got an
answer (a half-open connection, a proxy holding it) meant a picture that never appeared: the
gesture stayed pending for as long as the page lived. And even a failed transfer was only
resumed on a connect or on the transition back to ONLINE, both driven by the collab socket, so
a transfer that failed while the socket stayed up left the pendency PENDENTE, the feature
operation prepared, and the head-of-line hold of _loadOperations keeping every later edit on
this machine until something reconnected, which on a healthy socket can be hours.

Two changes:
- bulkUploadImages gets the push's deadline, sized from its body (uploadDeadlineMs over the
  body serialized once), so a hung request is cut and classified as a transient failure;
- blob-upload-queue schedules its own resumption after a transient failure while the connection
  is up (15 s, then 30 s, 60 s, 120 s, 300 s), one timer, reset on success and on a scope change;
  fired offline it does nothing, because the transition back to ONLINE already resumes at once.
  The resumption sends under the SAME id, which is what the server recognises as a retry.

Proof, tests/e2e-ui/subida-de-imagem-pendurada.repro.spec.js (the first bulk request is
intercepted and never answered, the WebSocket keeps working): before, the gesture was still
pending after 90 s, the feature never written, one request held (red); after, the held request
is cut at ~31 s, the feature is written, the resumption at 47 s passes, the feature and the
bytes are on the server under the same id, a line drawn afterwards traverses the full chain,
and the peer sees the image (green). browser-collab-imagem-retomada (3 cases) still passes.
Deterministic cases: blob-upload-queue.test.js (with the connection up, a transient failure is
resumed by itself under the same id and releases the operation, red with blob-upload-queue.js
reverted; offline the scheduled resumption sends nothing), sync-http-deadline.test.js (a 100 KB
bulk body is not cut at 30 s and is cut at its own deadline).

Pre-existing reds on the base, unrelated: teto-de-peso "o grafo COMPLETO" and
cauda-longa-vira-retrato "REST, no connect a partir do cursor duravel".

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(undo): undo and redo re-derive the analysis output from the resulting input

The history entry of a line-of-sight or viewshed edit (updateWithProcessed,
removeWithProcessed, moveBetweenMaps) kept the old output halves, and undo
and redo REINSERTED them. Since undo takes back only what its own edit
changed (keepLaterEdits, 1aeb1e6c), the input it leaves may carry a peer's
later geometry, and the reinserted halves were drawn on the old one: the
analysis showed in the wrong place on the author's screen. When the undo
changes nothing on the input (the peer redid every field) no op leaves, no
receipt comes back to re-derive through the inbound path, and the wrong
drawing stays until a reload.

Fix: a store op rederiveAnalysisOutput(inputType, id, mapName) (derived
write, no op, mapDocumentForDerivedWrite) is passed to the undo engine and
called after the input is restored in every one of the three action types,
instead of reinserting the kept copies. batchUpdateAnalysisFeatures also
stops recording an undo entry when the input did not change (the observer
field commits twice, on debounce and on blur, and the empty entry made the
next Ctrl+Z announce "desfeita" and do nothing).

Proof: browser-collab-analise-desfazer.repro.spec.js, two browsers: A traces
a line of sight and changes the observer height; B changes the height again
and drags the target endpoint; A undoes with the toolbar button. B's work
stays on the input and A's halves equal deriveAnalysisOutput(input), field by
field. Negative control: with store-state-manager.js reverted the spec is red
("o desfazer deixou no autor metades incoerentes com a feicao"). A first
version with only B's drag passed on the old code too: the undo op's receipt
re-derived the output a second later, which is why B now redoes every field.
undo-redo.test.js asserted the old call shape (three addFeature calls) and
now asserts one addFeature plus the re-derivation. Also green:
desfazer-preserva-edicao-do-par, browser-undo-redo, browser-p8-undo-local,
the two earlier analysis repros; vitest frontend.

Based on the cherry-picked copy of 1aeb1e6c (70f09062), which must not be
integrated twice.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(sync): a map setting received from a peer no longer makes the next edit of it a conflict

A map setting op (notes, grid, saved position, base layer, temporal config)
moves the MAP's revision on the server, but applyRemoteMapSettingOp left the
peer's map document with the confirmed revision it had before. The peer's next
edit of the same setting declared that stale base, and the server, which saw
the unit change after it, refused it: "Os mesmos campos foram alterados no
servidor." The edit vanished from the peer's disk (reverted to the server's)
and became a pending conflict, although the peer had already received and
displayed the change: a race lost against nobody. mergeRemoteMapUpdate already
clears the base for a plain map op for exactly this reason; the five setting
sub-types did not.

Fix: forgetConfirmedMapRevision clears the map document's confirmed revision
for a PEER's setting op (no base is the honest answer, as for map ops); the
author's own op re-applied (localRepair) keeps the revision its receipt
stamped.

Proof: notas-do-colega-recusada.repro.spec.js, two real browsers: B saves
notes, A receives them and corrects only the title through the panel. Before:
red (server kept "Notas do B"; A's op refused with status conflict, fields
["notas"], seen in A's queue issues). It stays red with only the notes-panel
fix applied, so it is independent of it. After: green, no issue in A's queue,
B receives A's title. Unit: it.each over four setting types (peer clears,
localRepair keeps). Map/temporal/lock collab specs (17) green.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(collab): a peer's saved map notes no longer open the notes panel on every screen

The MAP_NOTES branch of applyRemoteMapSettingOp emitted MAP_NOTES_REQUESTED
after storing a peer's notes. That event is the notes button's request to OPEN
the panel (sidebar _onMapNotesRequested collapses the sidebar, cleans up the
feature panel content and shows the notes), so every client, whatever it was
doing, got the peer's map notes thrown over its screen, with an Edit button
even for a read-only role (the event carries no readOnly), and a feature panel
open on another client was replaced by it.

Fix: a new EventTypes.MAP_NOTES_CHANGED ("refresh, never open"). The sidebar
redraws the notes panel only when it is already showing the notes of that map
and is not in edit mode (the person's unsaved text keeps the screen).

Proof: notas-do-colega-abre-painel.repro.spec.js, two real browsers, B saves
notes through the panel. Before: red (the notes panel appeared on A). After:
green; negative control (handler reverted) red. The existing case in
remote-operation-handler.test.js asserted the defect (it expected
MAP_NOTES_REQUESTED) and now expects MAP_NOTES_CHANGED and NOT the request.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(import): the file's own name and its reserved columns survive the import

extractAttributesFromImport skipped every reserved property name, case-insensitively since I8
(2026-09-21), so the <name> of every KML placemark and the NOME, NAME, ID, TYPE, SOURCE, TEXT,
SIZE, COLOR, LAYER, STATE... columns of a shapefile, GeoJSON or CSV vanished without a trace, and
every feature was born "Ponto #N". Measured in Chromium: a placemark named "Base Alfa" became
"Ponto #1"; a DBF with NOME/ID/TYPE kept only its non-reserved column.

Approved by the coordinator (product decision, 2026-09-23 night), because both halves only
preserve data that was being dropped, without changing a contract:
(a) the first non-empty nome/name (any casing) is the feature's name; "Ponto #N" is only the
    fallback. A later name key with the same value is consumed with it (our own KMZ writes
    <name> and an ExtendedData nome); a different one is kept.
(b) a reserved key that no import reader consumes is kept as `<key>_importado`, with a numeric
    suffix on collision, never overwriting a key of the file. The keys a reader consumes (the
    temporal columns, the trajectory) are still skipped, and no reserved spelling is ever written
    as an attribute key, which is the property I8 established and which stays asserted.

Test changed on purpose: tests/unit/user-data-atributos-de-importacao.test.js pinned the loss
("drops system properties", "the two paths now agree ... toEqual({})"). It now pins the new
contract: name to nome, reserved to <key>_importado, collision suffix, no _importado_importado on
a re-import, and, over every reserved name in three casings, never kept under a reserved name and
never lost unless a reader consumed it (vacuum control: more than 200 kept).

Proof in Chromium, tests/e2e-ui/importar-nome-e-chaves-reservadas.spec.js: a KML (name,
description, ExtendedData ID/TYPE) and a shapefile (NOME, ID, TYPE, OBS) dropped on the map and
read from the store. Negative control with the previous user_data_manager.js and import.control.js:
"Expected: Base Alfa, Received: Ponto #1", both cases red. The KMZ round trip is the next commit

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
perf(presence): cap the cursor at 5 frames per second at the origin, so presence fits a slow link

Every cursor item reaches every colleague in the room, about 260 bytes each, and the server
batches every 100 ms. With the client throttle at 80 ms (12.5 Hz), a peer's downlink carried
6.5 to 7.3 items per second per colleague moving the mouse. On the 40 kbps military link the
product targets (5000 B/s), measured with 60 Hz mouse input on the wire of a peer's socket:
3408 B/s with 2 colleagues moving (68% of the link) and 5639 B/s with 3 (113%: the link
saturated by cursors alone, with operations and the heartbeat pong queued behind them).

CURSOR_THROTTLE_MS goes from 80 to 200 ms (at most 5 Hz). The leading move still goes at once
and the last position of every window is still guaranteed (scheduleCoalesced, unchanged). The
origin is the one place that caps both the uplink of whoever moves and the downlink of everyone
who watches. After: 4.8 items per second per mover, 2518 B/s with 2 and 3710 B/s with 3.

Guards: tests/e2e-ui/presenca-cabe-no-link-lento.spec.js (the measurement above as a spec,
bound at 5.5 items/s per mover and at least 3 so a stopped cursor cannot pass; the baseline run
of the same harness on the parent measured 6.5 and 7.3, red); a deterministic case in
tests/integration/presence-bridge.test.js (a 60 Hz hand for 10 s sends at most 51 frames and
the last position goes out; red with the constant at 80). The existing cases now advance the
exported constant instead of a literal 80. presence-live-cursors and browser-sharing-presence
pass with the new rate.

Not enough on its own for 3+ colleagues at 40 kbps (74% of the link with 3); the next step is
adaptive and needs a decision, see the report.

fix(collab): socket frames that write or read the log re-check authorization first

The REST path checks live authorization on every request (strict `auth`
reads account, OM, session cut and role from the database;
requireAtlasPermission reads the share). The collaboration socket resolves

(~30 s) or when sharing changes. Deactivating the ACCOUNT or the OM, demoting
the global role or cutting the sessions reconciled no socket on the spot, so
for up to a whole sweep the owner of an open socket kept WRITING through
`operation`/`operations` and READING the log through `sync_request` with the
permission of before, while the same person was already refused over REST.

feature was written.

three frames that write or read the log; a socket that loses its authorization
is closed with 4003 before the handler runs. Presence frames stay on the sweep
(no atlas content, and a query per cursor frame would cost the hot path). Not
fail-closed: a transient database failure is counted as the sweep counts it.

commits.message:
fix(import): a Windows-1252 CSV, DBF or KML no longer loses every accent to U+FFFD

Every reader of an imported text file decoded it as UTF-8 whatever it was: file.text() for the
CSV, FileReader.readAsText for GeoJSON, KML and GPX, JSZip's 'string' for the KML inside a KMZ,
and shpjs for a DBF with no .cpg. The files people bring are often not UTF-8: a CSV saved by
Excel in pt-BR is Windows-1252, a Brazilian DBF is Windows-1252 with no .cpg, an older KML or GPX
declares encoding="ISO-8859-1". Every accented letter became U+FFFD in attribute names and
values and in the description ("Munic?pio: Bras?lia"), irreversibly once saved, locally and on
the server alike.

declared encoding decides; otherwise the bytes are UTF-8 when valid and Windows-1252 when not.
The readers now read bytes and decode through it. For a shapefile ZIP, a DBF with no .cpg whose
records are not valid UTF-8 gets a .cpg naming windows-1252 before shpjs runs
(_completarCpgDosDbf); the ZIP is returned untouched when no DBF needs it.

Proof, real Chromium through the real doors (the Importar tab's CSV option, a file dropped on
the map), read back from the store: tests/e2e-ui/importar-arquivo-codificacao-e-camadas.spec.js,
4/4 green (CSV 1252; CSV UTF-8 with BOM as control; DBF 1252 without .cpg; KML ISO-8859-1).

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(collab): the remote render gate opens on a watchdog and its trailing wait is capped

Review finding on 73d567ed (integrated as 4786cd8f): the single-flight gate of
wireRemoteFeatureRender was released only in the refresh's finally, with no deadline.
setupMapFeatures can wait on the network (a missing image blob goes to fetchImageBlob,
a plain fetch with no signal or deadline; the symbol library is a dynamic import), so
one stuck refresh (a peer pastes a photo on a 40 kbps link) stopped the 2D rendering of
EVERY later remote edit until F5. Before the gate each op armed an independent refresh
and the page recovered. Second half: the spacing was max(80, 2 x last refresh), wall
clock including network, never decaying and unbounded, applied to every schedule, so a
slow image delayed the next ISOLATED edit by minutes and the JSDoc promise of 80 ms
for a single operation was false.

Fix:
- REFRESH_WATCHDOG_MS (5 s): a refresh that has not settled releases the gate; the
  event that arrived meanwhile gets its refresh at the debounce; the late settlement
  of the stuck refresh is a no-op (release is keyed by run id), so it cannot open the
  gate held by a newer refresh.
- The spacing lives only on the TRAILING path (events that arrived during a refresh),
  equals the duration of the refresh that just ran, capped at 2 s. An isolated event
  always waits debounceMs (80 ms).

Tests (tests/unit/remote-feature-render.test.js): never-settling refresh released by
the watchdog; late settlement does not open the next run's gate; 160 s refresh ->
trailing wait 2000 ms; isolated event after a costly refresh -> 80 ms.
Negative controls: against 73d567ed 4 cases fail; watchdog release removed -> 2 fail;
cap removed -> 1 fails. Frontend suite and lint green (docs-integridade times out only
under the parallel full run, passes alone). Browser, --retries=0: transferencia-origem-
cheia (the case that failed 2 of 10 on its source instrument with the first version:
8 of 8 and 3 of 3 after), native-render, full-chain, pending edit survives remote op,
colar-imagem: 10 passed.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(sync): a durable cursor is only trusted by the principal it was staged for

The server cuts the snapshot by who asks: a read-level snapshot (public-link
visitor, Visualizador) carries no spatial comment, and catalog definitions pass
the caller's access predicate (getAtlasSnapshot). Since connect asks only for
the tail over a complete generation (_durablePullCursor), the generation staged
by an anonymous public visit counted as complete for the account that logged in
afterwards on the same machine (link, "Entrar", pick the atlas in "Meus Atlas":
no logged-out boot runs in between, so nothing sweeps the visit's namespace).
The owner then opened the atlas and never saw the comments made before the
visit. applyRemoteSnapshot's "same version, nothing to do" shortcut
(activeGenerationHolds) would also have skipped the owner's full snapshot.

The generation record now carries the principal of the SyncSession that staged
it (null for a visitor). _durablePullCursor refuses a cursor staged for another
principal, and activeGenerationHolds refuses the shortcut. A record written
before the field existed is trusted (only development machines have one).

Proof (Chromium, real backend): visita-publica-depois-conta-ve-tudo.repro.spec.js.
Without the fix: the owner sees no comment ([]). With it: the comment is there.
Two integration files asserted the exact three-field record; they now include
the principal.

fix(sync): let the pull deadline count silence, so a large atlas opens over a slow link

pullSync carried a 180 s deadline over the whole request, body included (f8e109ea, which also
contradicted the P6 note that the pull is left unbounded). On the 40 kbps link the product
targets, any snapshot or tail whose compressed body needs more than 180 s to arrive was cut on
every attempt while its bytes were still flowing, and the atlas could not be opened on that
link at all: a person joining an atlas with a few MB of surveyed geometry never got in.

_request gains deadlineCountsSilence: every chunk of the response body re-arms timeoutMs, read
through the body stream in _parseBody (text() when there is no stream). pullSync uses it: the
first byte still has 180 s (the server builds the snapshot before answering), a body that keeps
arriving is not cut, a body that stops arriving still is, 180 s after its last chunk.

opening an atlas of 130 surveyed tracks (5.37 MB decoded)
(tests/e2e-ui/retrato-em-link-lento.repro.spec.js): before, the snapshot answered 200 but its
body was cut at 184 s, the open never completed and none of the 130 features appeared in 420 s

negative control is that red run, made with api-client.js at the parent commit. Unit cases in

to the cap plus one row over idx_operations_atlas_version
(MEASURE_OPERATIONS_TAIL: count and sum of pg_column_size, the stored size,

stored, ~4 MB of JSON: stored was ~55% of the text for a polygon feature,
1.43 MB for 2.61 MB over 100 ops). Why each number is in the comment of its
constant. isSnapshot is already part of the contract on both doors (REST pull
of the connect, WS sync_request); approved by the coordinator.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
perf(collab): a peer applies a frame of remote creates with one write of the map document

Root cause: every remote feature op is a read-modify-write of the WHOLE map document
(all features of the map), and the peer applied the author's push frame one op at a
time (ws-client queued one apply per op). A burst of K creates on a map of N features
cost K full-document round trips: O(K*N).

Measured in Chromium, peer B receiving creates pushed in frames of 25 (shared, loaded
machine; apply span = first to last REMOTE_OPERATION_APPLIED on B):
- 300 creates on a map of 3000 points: 16.0-24.5 s (after the render fix) -> 1.4 / 2.4 s
- 500 creates on a map of 5000 points: 108.7 s with 21 s of long tasks -> 2.4 s, 0 long tasks
Per-op cost before: ~22 ms at ~250 features, 88 ms at ~2500, 217 ms at ~5250.

Fix: applyRemoteOperations(frame) keeps the single-op contract (in order, stop at the
first false, throws propagate) and writes consecutive plain feature CREATEs of one map
together (applyRemoteCreateRun): one getMap, one saveMap, then per member its version
record, FEATURE_CREATED, apply.persist span, REMOTE_OPERATION_APPLIED and deferred
completions. Any member needing a per-op branch (pending local edit, older version,
map not landed, the author's own echo, a cross-map move) sends the whole run back to
the single path before anything is written. ws-client hands a multi-op frame to an
'operationBatch' handler when the engine registered one; the gateway keeps the offline
gate and the Lamport advance.

Guard: tests/integration/rajada-remota-um-documento.repro.test.js (25 creates = 1 read
+ 1 write; each op keeps its events and version; pending edit, missing map, echo, move
and mixed frames fall back; write failure propagates) and two ws-client cases.
Negative control: disabling the run path fails 2 cases, disabling the frame handler
fails the 2 ws-client cases. sync-engine.test's wired-handler list gains
'operationBatch'. Frontend suite and lint green (docs-integridade and
idb-decisao4-medicao time out only under the parallel load, pass alone). 18 of 19
collab browser cases green; the 19th (transferencia-origem-cheia "trava REAL") failed
once on its instrument floor and passed 3 of 3 on rerun (see report).

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(sync): a peer's briefing envelope no longer erases a slide edit the server kept

The server stores each slide in its own row and applies slide ops one by one,
so two people editing DIFFERENT slides of one briefing at the same time both
land in Postgres. The peer, however, ignored live slide ops (EntityType.SLIDE
was an inbound no-op) and converged through the briefing envelope, which
carries its author's WHOLE slide list, built before the author knew of the
colleague's edit, and replaced the local list in bloc under LWW. The later
envelope erased the other person's slide edit from both clients' disks while
the server kept it, until the next F5; an export or "Salvar como local" in
that window wrote the stale text out.

Fix: an UPDATE envelope decides the briefing's own fields and the slide ORDER
only (mergeEnvelopeSlides): a slide in both keeps this client's content, a
slide only in the envelope is not taken from it (its own CREATE brings it, and
the envelope's copy may be one the colleague deleted), a slide only here stays
last (the server's rule for a slide missing from slide_order). Live slide ops
are applied per slide through applyLocalSlideIntent (keeping the slide's
position; the server's snake_case aliases stripped), and SLIDE joins
CONVERGENCE_GUARDED so each slide gets its own defer/version guard.

Proof: briefing-slides-concorrentes.repro.spec.js, two real browsers, B's sync
POST held by page.route while A edits another slide (deterministic
interleaving). Before: red, A's title back to the old text on A and B,
Postgres with A's. After: 3/3 green in series; negative control (handler
reverted) red. Unit: new describe in remote-operation-handler.test.js (stale
envelope, order, no resurrection, per-slide LWW, delete). Updated tests: the
envelope-only control case now sends the slide op too; SLIDE moved from FORA
to DENTRO in convergence-guarded-decisao-por-tipo with the reason; the map
page source ceiling 11710 -> 11730 kB (11713 measured, no new module, see the
comment). Briefing specs 22/22 green; contract e2e briefing-full,

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(export): off-screen export map no longer hangs forever on a failed source

The PDF export (single sheet and mosaic) and the Garmin KMZ export draw an
off-screen MapLibre map from the live map's style and await `idle` / `load`
on it with no deadline. That style carries every catalog source, data and
analysis layers included, visible or not. A vector, raster or raster-dem
source whose TileJSON request fails sets `_loaded = true` and fires `error`,
but no `data` event, so MapLibre schedules no new frame. When that failure is
the last thing the off-screen map is waiting for, the map has already stopped
rendering, never re-evaluates `loaded()` and never fires `load` nor `idle`:
the progress modal sat on "Enquadrando area..." for 300 s, in the Vite dev
server and in the production bundle over HTTPS alike. Measured in the
browser: 10 to 20 renders, then none; one manual `triggerRepaint()` fired
`load`, `idle` and the rest of the export at once.

It is not a test-only condition: the catalog seeded by the migrations points
four sources at `http://localhost/tiles/...` placeholders until an
administrator replaces them, and a tile server that is down, slow to refuse,
or answers 401/404 produces the same failed TileJSON.

`repaintOnSourceError` (export-utils.js) schedules one repaint per `error` of
the off-screen map, called right after construction in the three exporters.

Proof: tests/e2e-ui/exportacao-com-fonte-que-falha.spec.js refuses the
catalog TileJSON 4 s late (the losing interleaving, made deterministic) and
expects the PDF download, single sheet and 1x2 mosaic. Before: 2/2 red
(120 s waiting for the download). After: 2/2 green, 8/8 in series with
--repeat-each=4 --retries=0. Negative control (helper without the repaint):
2/2 red again.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(collab): escalate the heartbeat tolerance, so a slow downlink converges instead of looping

The client heartbeat closed the collab socket when a pong was overdue at its second tick
(25 to 50 s). The browser delivers a WebSocket message only when the whole frame has arrived,
and the server's pong travels behind whatever it queued first on the same TCP stream. On the
40 kbps link the product targets, a 324 KB frame (one detailed feature a colleague imported,
or the sync_response replay of what this client missed) takes about 65 s. The socket was cut
mid-frame, the reconnect asked sync_request from the same cursor, the server queued the same
frame, and the heartbeat cut it again: that peer never converged, forever.

Now a heartbeat close doubles the number of overdue ticks the next socket may wait (16 ticks,
400 s, at most), and a pong answered within its own tick brings it back to one; a new
connect() starts strict. While the pong is overdue the ping keeps going up every tick, because
the server reaps a socket that sent nothing for a whole 30 s sweep and its own protocol ping
is stuck behind the same frame. A dead link is still closed.

Proof, tests/e2e-ui/ws-quadro-grande-em-link-lento.repro.spec.js (Chromium, server-to-client
frames delivered in order at 5000 B/s through routeWebSocket): before, 5 sockets in 240 s,
"heartbeat timeout" every ~51 s, the 324 KB sync_response never delivered (red); after, 2
sockets, one cut, the 324 KB sync_response delivered at 117.5 s (green). The interleaving is
deterministic in tests/integration/ws-heartbeat-quadro-grande.repro.test.js (fake clock and
socket): 3 of 4 cases red with ws-client.js reverted; the fourth, the dead-link bound, is
green on both sides on purpose.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(sync): a 413 halves the push cut and is stored with a pt-BR reason

Review follow-up to f79cf3a4, two defects in how the flush handled a 413:

1. The stored reason was error.message, i.e. the Express default "request
   entity too large" or, from a proxy answering with HTML, "HTTP 413", and the
   pending list shows the stored reason verbatim; the warning was the generic
   one. Retrying the same bytes gets the same 413, so the reason (and the
   warning) is now CORPO_GRANDE_DEMAIS, next to LOTE_GRANDE_DEMAIS, naming the
   only thing that helps: split the import into smaller parts.

2. After a 413 caused by the SUM of a batch, the isolation mode stayed on for
   the rest of the flush, sending every remaining op alone (up to 25x the
   pushes). A 413 is about the bytes, not about one op, so it now HALVES the
   cut until it fits and keeps it there; only an indivisible piece (a single
   op, or a logical batch peek will not split) that still gets 413 becomes a
   durable issue, after which the cut goes back to full. 400/422 keep the
   one-op isolation, which is right for a poison op.

Tests (frontend/tests/integration/sync-engine.test.js): 25 ops that fit 6 per
body push as [25, 12, 6, 6, 6, 6, 1] with nothing refused; a lone oversized op
is stored with the pt-BR reason (no HTTP/entity wording) and the same sentence
is the warning; an indivisible 3-op gesture that 413s is refused whole while
the loose op behind it goes out. Negative control: disabling the halving turns
the four 413 cases red. api-client-error-contract.test.js pins that a 413 with
an nginx HTML body, and the backend's JSON 413, both reach the engine as an
ApiError with status 413. Also fixes the {400, 422} comment in
tests/e2e/lote-estado-do-servidor.e2e.test.js.

commits.message:
perf(collab): a burst of peer operations no longer rebuilds every map source per operation

Root cause: wireRemoteFeatureRender rebuilt ALL feature sources from the store
(setupMapFeatures: full map document read plus setData of every collection, then a
LAYERS_CHANGED round) 80 ms after each remote feature event, and nothing stopped a
rebuild from starting while the previous one ran. On a map of a few thousand
features, applying one remote operation takes longer than 80 ms (whole-document read
and write), so the timer fired between nearly every two operations.

Measured in Chromium, peer B receiving 300 remote creates (12 pushes of 25) on a map
of 3000 points, three interleaved runs each on a shared, loaded machine:
- before: 161 / 220 / 176 rebuilds, convergence 35.9 / 44.7 / 33.4 s
- after:   45 /  52 /  50 rebuilds, convergence 24.5 / 18.7 / 16.0 s

Fix: a refresh never overlaps another; an event arriving during one marks the sources
dirty and schedules exactly one more when it ends; the wait is max(80 ms, 2x the last
refresh), so the rebuild takes at most a third of a sustained burst and a single op
still draws after 80 ms. unwire also stops the trailing reschedule.

Guard: five new cases in tests/unit/remote-feature-render.test.js count scheduled
timers (no clock). Negative control: with the previous module three of them fail.

feature-mutations, all-types, full-chain, scale, three-client-flow, pending edit

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(undo): undoing a feature edit no longer reverts what a peer changed after it

An undo entry for a feature edit holds the whole feature before and after
(recordAction type 'update'), and _executeUndoAction wrote the whole "before"
back through updateFeature. When a peer changed another field of the same
feature between the edit and the Ctrl+Z, the "before" carried the OLD value of
that field and the undo wrote it back. The op leaves the client with an
up-to-date base (the peer's edit was already received), so the server has
nothing to call disputed and applies it: the peer's work is gone on every
client and in Postgres. Undo is local per person (P8); it must only take back
what this edit did.

Fix: updateFeature accepts { revertFrom } (undo and redo only). Inside the map
document lock, keepLaterEdits builds the target from `to` but keeps the
current value of every field (geometry as a whole, each top-level property)
whose current value is no longer what the reverted edit left there. Applied
to 'update' and 'updateWithProcessed', in both directions.

Proof: desfazer-preserva-edicao-do-par.repro.spec.js, two real browsers, all
gestures through the UI (A draws and recolors, B renames, A undoes with the
toolbar button, the same door as Ctrl+Z). Before: red (name back to
"Linha #1" on A, B and the server). After: green; negative control
(store-state-manager reverted) red again. Unit: keepLaterEdits cases. Two
existing tests asserted the exact old call shape and were updated to the new
one (undo-redo.test.js, desfazer-escrita-de-propriedade.repro.test.js). Undo
specs browser-p8-undo-local, browser-undo-redo, symbol-selector-undo,
browser-context-move and engineering-symbol-lifecycle pass (8/8).
