commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(collab): the sync_request answer reaches the peer before any op it does not carry

The client applies socket frames in arrival order (`_queueApply`), and only
the CONVERGENCE_GUARDED entity types drop an op older than one already
applied; map updates, group membership, comments, slides and catalog layers
are applied blindly. handleSyncRequest read the tail, did one more read, and
only then sent the answer: an op committed in that gap and broadcast before
the send reached the peer FIRST, and the answer, carrying the previous op of
the same entity, was applied over it. A peer reconnecting (lost connection,
socket killed by backpressure) while a colleague renamed a map kept the older
name until a full snapshot, with nothing on either side flagging it.

Operation frames addressed to the socket are now HELD from the start of its
sync_request until the answer is out, then released after it, dropping every
op the answer already covers (per atlas, version order is commit order, so an
op at or below the highest covered version is in the answer or below the
client's cursor; resending it would replay an older op over a newer one). The
hold lives in the per-socket boundary (collab.send.js), so released frames go
through the same prune; presence and control frames are never held.

Repro: tests/ws/sync-request-ordem-dos-quadros.repro.test.js wraps db.query to
PAUSE the pull's second read while a colleague renames the map: red before
(frames "operations, sync_response", applied name "Nome 1" vs "Nome 2" on the
server), green after; negative control = removing holdOperationFrames brings
the red back. The release filter, which the socket test cannot force, is
pinned by tests/unit/quadros-de-op-retidos-no-sync-request.test.js.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(sync): REST markers take the per-atlas log lock, so version order stays commit order

The incremental pull cursor (`server_version > cursor`) is sound only if, per
atlas, nextval order equals commit order; pushOperations guaranteed that with
a per-atlas advisory lock. The REST exceptions that write a structural marker
into an EXISTING atlas (map duplicate, map merge) did not take it, and the
duplicate also updates atlas.map_order (row lock) BEFORE writing its marker.
A push arriving in between drew the LOWER version, blocked on the atlas row
inside trg_update_atlas_version, and committed AFTER the marker: a peer that
pulled in that window stored the marker's version as its cursor and never
received the push's op; and the trigger then wrote the lower version over
current_version, moving the atlas version backwards.

The lock now has one definition, lockAtlasLog (src/modules/sync/atlas-log-lock.js),
taken by the push, the duplicate and the merge FIRST, before any write (the
same order the push uses, so no deadlock). The merge gains it too, which also
closes the window between its locked-map check and a push that locks a map.

Repro: tests/integration/marcador-rest-ordem-de-commit.repro.test.js forces
the losing interleaving with test-only triggers scoped to one atlas and map
(each step waits for the previous one to be seen in pg_locks): red before
("a op do push (v2) ficou abaixo do cursor 3"), green after; negative control
= removing the duplicate's lockAtlasLog call brings the red back. Reachable
only through the API: this client never calls duplicate or merge.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(sync): derive the line-of-sight and viewshed output on every client

In an atlas of the server the analysis OUTPUT (processed_los,
processed_visibility, the green and red halves) never reached anyone. Its id
is `<inputId>-visible` / `-obstructed`, not a UUID, so the server refused
every output op ("identificador ou valor com formato invalido"). The input
layers are painted with zero opacity, so the output is the only visible
drawing: the peer never saw the analysis, the author kept "Recusas: 2"
forever, and the refusal-triggered resync wiped the output from the author's
own store even before any F5. No test caught it because every sync test
seeded processed_* with a UUID, which is not the id the tools produce.

Decision of 2026-09-23 (coordinator): the output is derived per client and
never travels, like the color counts and the regenerated symbol raster.
- store/analysis-output.js: one pure leaf, deriveAnalysisOutput, now used
  by both geometry classes (generateProcessedFeatures delegates) and by the
  inbound path; DERIVED_OUTPUT_BUCKET_OF in the type registry is the one list.
- feature.operations stamps the bucket (`storage`) on every feature op
  description; the dispatcher drops derived-output writes BY TYPE (not by id
  shape) before the "un-pushable" refusal, so a non-UUID id of any other type
  still goes out and is refused loudly.
- remote create/update/delete of los/visibility and the move cascade
  re-derive or remove the output; the snapshot discards server output rows
  (legacy uploads with random UUIDs) and re-derives.
- the upload of a local atlas skips the output buckets (not counted as lost).

Proof: browser-collab-analise-derivada.repro.spec.js (two browsers, real
tools on synthetic terrain): peer sees both analyses field by field, no
refusal, no output row on the server, both survive F5, deleting the line on
the author removes its halves on the peer. 5/6 green in series (the one red
was a one-shot read after F5, now a poll; see the hunt report). Negative
control: with the src changes reverted the spec fails at the author's own
output (processed_los 2 -> 0). Unit: saida-de-analise-derivada (absolute
split, author x peer equivalence on one corpus, census of the `storage`
stamp); integration: saida-de-analise-nao-viaja. Tests that asserted the old
contract (outputs uploaded / swept by all-types, viewshed throwing on bad
cellData) were updated with the reason written next to them.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(sync): size the push deadline from its body, so a slow link can upload a large batch

pushOperations (and the legacy receipt lookup) carried a FIXED 30 s deadline since f8e109ea,
over the whole request. On the 40 kbps military link the product targets, 30 s uploads about
150 KB, so a larger batch (an imported file, a long track, a detailed polygon, or simply a
gesture batch the queue must send whole) was aborted mid-upload on every attempt. The server
never saw it, the queue re-peeked the same head batch, and every later edit of that person in
that atlas stayed stuck behind it, forever. The code comments still promised the push was
unbounded (P6), which is what the deadline had silently undone.

The deadline is now 30 s plus the body's upload time at 2000 B/s (16 kbps, 2.5x below the
specified link), computed by the pure uploadDeadlineMs. fetch exposes no upload progress, so a
stall timer is not available for the request side.

Proof, Chromium with CDP throttling at 5000 B/s restricted to the backend origin
(tests/e2e-ui/push-em-link-lento.repro.spec.js): a 324 KB create needs ~65 s. Before: attempts
at 0.9 s, 32.4 s, 66.9 s, 102.9 s, each cut with no response, row never on the server, the
small edit made afterwards never either (red). After: 200 at 67.6 s, then the small edit
(green). Negative control: reverting api-client.js turns the spec red again with the same
attempt pattern. Unit cases in tests/integration/sync-http-deadline.test.js pin the sizing
(a 324 KB push still in flight at 90 s, cut only at its own deadline; edge cases NaN,
Infinity, negative, non-number; the receipt lookup sized the same way).

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(briefing): the open editor no longer saves its stale copy over a peer's work

The briefing editor read the briefing once on open and every autosave wrote
updateBriefing(id, { slides: this._briefing.slides }), the whole in-memory
list. It never followed remote updates, so after a peer changed the briefing
the store diffed that stale list against the fresh document on disk and
derived slide ops from the difference: the slide the peer created became a
SLIDE DELETE and the title the peer rewrote went back to the old text, and
both were applied by the server. No race needed: two people with the same
briefing open, the one with the older copy touching anything (even only the
briefing name) after the peer's edit.

Fix: a three-way merge. The editor keeps a baseline (the store document its
copy was last reconciled with); diffBriefingEdits sends only the fields the
person changed (per slide, settings per key), and applyBriefingEdits applies
that patch over the document read inside the transaction. rebaseBriefingEdits
reconciles the copy with the store IN PLACE, keeping unsaved edits and every
slide object alive, and the editor now follows BRIEFING_UPDATED to show a
peer's slides. The slide import appends to the fresh list (appendSlides)
instead of saving the editor's copy plus the new slides.

Keeping the slide objects alive also fixes a single-user loss: after deleting
another slide or reordering, the slide form kept the OLD slide object
(this._briefing was replaced by a fresh read without re-rendering), so typing
in the title afterwards was never saved.

Proof: briefing-editor-copia-velha.repro.spec.js, two real browsers. Before:
2/2 red (slide "Dois" tombstoned in Postgres and gone from both disks; title
of "Um" reverted on the server). After: 2/2 green; negative control (editor
reverted) 2/2 red again. Unit: briefing-editor-mescla.test.js (includes the
autosave-window case the browser cannot pin). The 21 briefing specs
(browser-briefing-*, briefing-*, browser-collab-briefing-temporal,
quill-html-colado) pass.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(atlas): the anonymous public visit asks before emptying a rescued slot

A session that dies with pending work is rescued by adoptRemoteAtlasAsLocal,
which moves the claim of remote-<atlasId> to the local registry and zero
bytes: the rescued local atlas IS that namespace. The account door
(openRemoteAtlas) asks confirmDiscardingRescuedWork before emptying it, but
the anonymous branch of openPublicAtlasFromUrl (index.js) activated the same
namespace and called clearAllDataStore without asking. Any edit made in the
rescued local atlas after the rescue (a local atlas logs no operation, so no
queue carries it) was erased by opening the public link of the same atlas,
and the slot stayed in the list under its rescue name without it.

The public door now asks the same question after the claim and before any
write. Cancel keeps the tab on the atlas it had mounted and drops the link
from the address bar; "Apagar e abrir" releases the rescue after the remote
claim is registered and empties the queue too, as at the other door. The
ephemeral token is set only once the visit really goes ahead.

Proof (Chromium, real backend): visita-publica-poupa-resgate.repro.spec.js.
Before: the edit made in the rescued slot is gone after the visit and no
question is asked. After: 2/2 green. Negative control: reverting index.js
turns both cases red again.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(sync): a 413 on push shrinks the batch instead of freezing the queue forever

The /sync body is capped (10 MB express.json in backend/src/app.js, plus the
client_max_body_size of every proxy on the path). The flush treated only 400
and 422 as "these bytes will be refused forever"; 413 fell to the transient
branch, so a batch whose serialized size crossed the cap (importing a detailed
vector file is the common road) was resent with backoff for good, the whole
queue of that person stopped behind it (head-of-line), and the warning said
the connection was to blame and the edits would go out when it came back.

413 is a function of the size of the bytes, exactly like 400/422 are of their
content, so it joins PERMANENT_PUSH_REJECTIONS: the isolation mode shrinks the
batch, a batch that only overflows as a SUM drains op by op with nothing
discarded, and only a piece too large on its own becomes a durable issue with
the existing warning.

Repro (client): two cases in tests/integration/sync-engine.test.js, red before
(flush rejects, nothing dequeued), green after; negative control = the same two
cases with 413 removed from the set. Server contract pinned by
backend/tests/integration/sync-corpo-grande-413.test.js (a real HTTP socket
posting 11 MB gets 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE; measured 11/13/20/40 MB on loopback).

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
perf(sync): the outbound queue reads its keys by range, not by walking the whole database

Root cause: the queue database keeps more than envelopes. Every envelope brings an
identity and a head record, and FEATURE_LATEST is KEPT after the ack, one per feature
this client ever wrote in the atlas. countByState (run on every 1.5 s auto-flush tick),
peek and dequeue (once per push of 25) listed keys with localforage keys(), a cursor
over the WHOLE database, one callback per key.

Measured in Chromium (machine shared with ~30 node processes), OperationQueue on a real
IndexedDB, drain loop = peek(25) + dequeue until empty, no network:
- 2000 ops: drain 9.0 s -> 1.9 s; idle tick after drain 10-20 ms -> 0.3 ms
- 8000 ops: drain 75.3 s -> 9.4 s (was quadratic: 4x ops, 8x time);
  idle tick with the queue EMPTY and 8001 metadata keys 40 ms -> 0.3 ms, forever.

Fix: listKeysWithPrefix reads one IDBKeyRange (getAllKeys) per prefix through the shared
native connection, falling back to the filtered full listing for non-IndexedDB stores
and on any native failure. _getOrderedKeys, dequeue and countByState (op_, ISSUE, STATE)
use it; dequeue reads the matched envelopes in parallel.

Guard: tests/integration/fila-nao-varre-metadado.repro.test.js runs census, peek,
dequeue and the end-of-flush projection on fake-indexeddb with 300 leftover
FEATURE_LATEST keys and asserts zero keys() calls and zero cursors, plus the answers.
Negative control: with the old listing the two structural cases fail (keys called 4x
and 1x). Frontend suite, lint, 4 queue contract e2e files and 4 queue/collab browser
specs green.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(atlas): clone and map duplicate realign properties.layerId with the new layer

cloneMapSubEntities mints a new id for every layer and remaps the
features.layer_id COLUMN, but copied `properties` verbatim. A feature written
by the real client carries properties.layerId equal to the column, and the
snapshot serves properties from the JSONB without rewriting layerId from the
column (transformFeaturesToFrontend). So every feature of a server-side copy
("Copiar no servidor") reached the client naming a layer that exists only in
the SOURCE atlas. The client decides layer membership by the property (the
MapLibre visibility filter `['in', coalesce(layerId,'default'), visibleIds]`,
the features tab, hide/lock), so the copy opened with its features stored on
the server and invisible on the map. Import already realigned the property
(propriedadesRealinhadas); clone and duplicate did not.

Repro: tests/integration/copia-realinha-camada-da-feicao.repro.test.js pushes
a feature through /sync exactly as the client does, clones and duplicates, and
reads the snapshot: before the fix the clone and duplicate cases fail with the
source layer id; after, all three pass.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
feat(meteorologia): PITCIC weather forecast at a point, on a shell shared with the light panel

A context-menu entry, "Meteorologia neste ponto", opens a panel with the
forecast rows of the PITCIC weather matrix (EB70-MC-10.336, Quadro 4-5)
for D, D+1 and D+2 in Brasilia time: weather, precipitation and its
probability, max/min temperature, wind (bearing as the manual writes it,
mean speed), max gust, max/min humidity and min visibility, plus cloud
cover and pressure in a collapsed block. "Salvar tabela" saves a CSV.

- The BROWSER queries an Open-Meteo API directly (owner's decision); the
  backend makes no outbound call and only serves features.meteorologia
  (ON by default, owner's decision) and services.meteorologiaUrl
  (METEOROLOGIA_URL, the public API by default), both overridable in the
  admin Sistema tab. The request carries no credential, no Referer and
  nothing for the disk cache, with the point rounded to 0.1 deg; the
  Origin header and the egress address still reach the source, which only
  a source installed inside the network avoids.
- The model is pinned (gfs_seamless), the only global model probed that
  delivers every row for 16 days. Every request has a timeout, and the run
  metadata travels in parallel with the forecast.
- Days are cut in P and checked by an independent path: the same GFS run
  recorded hourly in UTC and as the source's own daily aggregates in
  Brasilia's zone must agree. Wind direction is the speed-weighted vector
  mean. Negative controls: a UTC day cut fails 9 cases, the unweighted
  direction 5, credentials 'include' 2, a serial fetch 1.
- The light and weather panels share one shell (card, phone sheet, pin,
  day controls, download; one panel per map), and hora-brasilia.js moved
  to utilities/ so neither panel imports the other. The light panel was
  compared by capture before and after: identical pixel for pixel in 7 of
  8 images, 4 px of antialiasing in the eighth.
- A spinner while the forecast travels; on failure, only the notice and
  "Tentar de novo", never a table of placeholders.
- Usage event meteorologia.aberta in both vocabularies, with migration
  016_uso_meteorologia.sql redeclaring the whole CHECK.

Left for later (docs/wiki/meteorologia-pitcic.md and the proposal): the
temperature gradient, which waits for a threshold from a smoke/CBRN
manual; the climate regime beyond the forecast's reach; cloud ceiling.

Verified: root lint; frontend suite 15768/15768; backend suite 5632/5633
on the previous code state, the one failure (images-gaps.test.js, a process
crash under load, a file this change does not touch) passing 24/24 alone
three times; Playwright captures at 1440 and 360 px read in Chromium and
Firefox. Committed at the owner's request before the contract e2e leg of
the final root run finished.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(telemetry): a logged-in user's usage batch survives the next page load

The usage queue across page loads (2026-09-12) deleted, on the first flush of
every load, each stored batch of another identity and counted it as a
failure. The four pages install telemetry before restoring the session, so
every logged-in load starts with a null identity, and the deleted batch was
the one the previous page wrote on `pagehide`. Measured in both browsers
with a 503 on the exit batch: 0/3 arrived for a logged-in user against 3/3
for an anonymous one; every logged-in navigation reported two collection
failures; and with the token in its last 30 s the exit flush triggered a
refresh inside `pagehide` and the fetch never left.

- A batch of another identity is skipped, never deleted, and the skip is not
  a failure; cleanup stays with the 24 h validity and the cap of 30, which
  now counts every stored batch. An account batch with no credential to
  carry is skipped too, and 401/409 on an account batch keep it for the next
  resume; on an anonymous batch they stay final.
- Owner decision Q2: only the explicit Sair gesture deletes an account's
  pending batches (announced by `confirmLogoutWithPendingWork`); page
  changes, boot and a session lost without a gesture keep them.
- A settling session resends its batches at once; the exit flush uses the
  in-memory token without renewing; usage and presence POSTs read the 204
  body, because cancelling it is exactly what Chromium logs as ERR_ABORTED.
- Wiki: the usage queue now holds for logged-in users too, and
  `indisponivel.visto` arrives late on a server outage instead of dying.

Verified: the browser repro 3/3 in Chromium and Firefox after the fix (0/3
before), collection failures per logged navigation 0 (2 before), 17 of 18
mutations turn a guard red (the survivor is unreachable and declared), root
lint and root npm test on the whole batch, and an independent review whose
findings were applied.

fix(boot): a failed server-atlas open no longer erases the queue or a local slot

When `?atlas=` failed after the namespace was mounted, the boot chain fell
into `enterLocalMapOnBoot` or `openAtlasChooserOnBoot`, and both emptied the
mounted scope with `clearAllDataStore()` defaults (`clearQueue` follows
`markLocal`). Reproduced in both browsers: the pending queue of the atlas
went from 1 operation to 0 and the next open did not deliver the edit; the
tab was left dead (remote scope, local origin, writes refused); and, since
the wipe read the installation-wide origin marker, a LOCAL slot was erased
on F5 when another tab had opened a server atlas.

- Owner decision Q1: a failed open preserves the queue and pending bytes and
  drops only the view. The chooser only navigates, carrying the reason in
  `?aviso=`; the local-map fallback enters the local slot through the live
  switch (`enterLocalAtlasOnBoot`), claimed with the mount witness.
- The probable cause of the 2026-09-22 matrix failure: `dropAtlasDatabases`
  now awaits the epoch mirror removal (a logout from atlas.html navigated
  before it and the next open restored the discard and aborted);
  `registerRemoteAtlas` reconciles durable pointers before reading the
  fence; the sync badge re-renders when the origin turns local (every failed
  open used to leave it frozen on "sem conexão"); the three non-map pages
  clear the local-map intent on logout; `getSyncProtocol` gets a 30 s
  deadline; the boot probe names a failed open.

fix, every new guard negative-controlled, root lint and root npm test on the

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
perf(boot): fire the persistent-storage request and stop awaiting it

The map boot awaited `pedirPersistencia` with a 2000 ms deadline. In
Firefox, `navigator.storage.persist()` opens a permission prompt, so every
boot of a user who had not answered it paid the whole deadline, on every
load and on every atlas switch by reload. Half of the users are on Firefox.

Awaiting bought nothing: the grant covers the whole origin, including what
the store already wrote, so asking before the store opens its databases was
never a precondition. `index.js` now fires the request and moves on. The
outcome becomes `pendente` at the moment of the request (so the boot line
never reads null, which means "this page never asked") and corrects itself
when the browser answers.

Measured in real Firefox, five boots each, with the old await restored only
for the comparison: warm boots from 3741-4174 ms down to 1648-2138 ms (cold
6887 to 5423 ms). Chromium unchanged at 1178-1296 ms warm.

Guard: pedido-de-persistencia-no-boot.test.js fails if `index.js` awaits
the request again, and if the outcome is null while the prompt is open;
both negative-controlled. Owner decision recorded in decisions-2026.md.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(modals): never hide an overlay that still holds focus

Cancelling the military symbol modal made Chrome report "Blocked
aria-hidden on an element because its descendant retained focus". The
"Configurar Simbolo" button is disabled while the symbol tables load,
Chrome drops focus from a disabled button, so show() saved
document.body as the opener. On close, body.focus() did nothing, and
ModalBase.hide only blurred when no opener had been saved, so focus
stayed on Cancelar while aria-hidden went on. hide() now blurs whenever
focus is still inside the overlay after the restore attempt; the fix is
in the base, so every modal gets it.

The probe that measured it found a second defect in the same modal: a
fresh SymbolSelectorModal per open, without destroyOnHide, left its
hidden overlay and its document keydown listener behind (1, 2 and 3
overlays after three opens). It is the only one of the three symbol
selectors that lacked the option.

Measured with a temporary Playwright probe against the real app and
backend: before, focus stuck on Cancelar in 3 of 3 rounds; after, focus
outside the modal in 6 of 6 and zero overlays left. The headless shell
does not emit the aria-hidden warning itself, so focus position is the
signal. The node repro fails on the old hide() and passes on the new.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
feat(tablet): the product answers to a finger, and a ruler measures whether it does

Until today the only layer that exercised the UI ran in a desk context, so the whole
touch half of the product was verified by READING code. This lot fixes what that
reading, and then a real measurement, turned up across the four surfaces.

THE RULER REPLACES THREE HAND-WRITTEN LISTS. The report asked for small targets to be
fixed by inventory ("a 16 by 16 div" in 3D, "three targets" in 360, "seven" in first
person). Opened, most of those were not targets at all: the crosshair carries
`pointer-events: none`, the thumbnail is decoration, the key pad is a keyboard hint.
`alvos-de-toque.tablet.spec.js` measures the BOX of every actionable element on the four
surfaces and fails below 44px, printing what it measured on stdout. It found exactly one
offender in the whole product: the search field at 42px, on every screen. It also caught
itself once: an ancestor with `display: none` zeroes a child's box without zeroing its
`display`, so the 3D bar was being skipped while the case passed.

THE MAP. Undo and redo existed only as Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y, which on a tablet is no door at
all. Both got a toolbar button, and the rule moved out of the keyboard into
`map/undo-redo.runner.js`, whose re-entrancy guard is per MODULE: with two doors, a
per-caller flag lets a tap during a running shortcut fire both, and the second undoes what
the first just did. A group popup now lays out as a LIST under a coarse pointer, because
in the grid the button is an icon plus a badge carrying the KEYBOARD shortcut, with the
name living in `title`, which is a hover bubble and never appears on a tablet.

THE 360. Seven fixes, and the costliest was one of ORDER: `assignHitRadii` ran before POIs
and comments joined the list, so only the navigation arrows got the fingertip floor. The
other two fell back to `radius * 1.5` with NO floor, which is why it stayed quiet: a POI at
the default size offered 36px of diameter, and `markerSize` 6 offered 18. Alongside: an
absolute floor for coarse pointers, the drag threshold read from `pointerType` (5px for
everyone meant a tap on an arrow was read as a drag and navigation simply did not happen),
the missing `pointercancel`, the finger that stopped turning the sphere after a pinch, the
pinch that zoomed the photo behind a comment card, `touch-action` moved out of an inline
style on the CONTAINER (where it is inherited, killing card scrolling) and onto the
canvases, and a Touch tab in the help, which offered only Mouse and Keyboard.

THE 3D. `scene.pick` searched for a target in THREE pixels, the ruler of a mouse. Reading
the code found three sites; the census found SIX, and the three missed were the measurement
and viewshed selections. The 3D measurement closed by right click or double click, so on a
tablet it could be started and not finished; it got the same finish button as the 2D tools,
through the same helper. And a tileset's `cacheBytes` was a flat 1 GB; it now comes from
`services/orcamento-de-memoria.js`, which drops to 256 MB when the machine declares 4 GB or
4 cores and does NOT drop when there is no clue, since Firefox and Safari publish no
`deviceMemory`.

FIRST PERSON. Looking around moved from mouse events to pointer events, and the drag
stopped reading `movementX`, which is optional on a touch pointer: where the browser does
not fill it, it reads zero and the camera simply does not turn, with no error. It now
measures the difference between two `clientX`. Walking did not exist at all there, since
WASD, the arrows, Space and Shift are absent on a tablet: `walk/touch-stick.js` is an
analogue stick plus jump and crouch, and the walker scales speed by the vector's magnitude,
which leaves the keyboard identical because two keys already saturate the cap. The
immersive button asks for Pointer Lock and now disappears under a coarse pointer, since
there is no pointer to capture and nothing the person could unlock. The loading bar was a
two-second `@keyframes` that finished full with 18 MB still to come; the body is now read
as a stream and the bar says how many MB of how many, staying indeterminate when there is
no `Content-Length` instead of inventing a position.

TWO DEFECTS CAME FROM READING THE CAPTURE, not from a test: the stick's knob escaped its
base at the end of the travel, and the key-hints card sat in the opposite corner telling the
person to use a keyboard they do not have, next to the control just born to replace it.

VERIFIED: root lint exit 0; frontend 755 files and 13809 cases; the tablet Playwright config
9 passed. Negative control on every logic fix, by exit code. The four red cases in the root
run belong to another session's in-flight `session-context.js` and `account.control.js`,
which are NOT in this commit.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(touch): give the edit handle a hit box instead of a single point

A HANDLE IS 16px ACROSS and was queried with ONE POINT. Hitting it meant landing
inside eight pixels of radius, against a fingertip that covers about 34; vertex
and midpoint handles alternate along the geometry, so a finger covers two or
three at once and `queryRenderedFeatures` answered for none of them. The doubled
touch tolerance already lived in `feature-hit-test.helpers.js` and was spent only
on FEATURE selection — sixteen call sites across twelve tools passed the raw
point.

`handleHitBox` is square because that is what MapLibre takes: a pair of corners,
everything intersecting the rectangle. Its corner is slightly more generous than
its edge, which costs nothing here — the nearest neighbouring handle sits more
than a tolerance away, and when it does not, the winner is the order MapLibre
returns, which is already top-down in the drawing. It does not depend on zoom or
projection on purpose: a handle is screen drawing with a fixed pixel radius, so
the slack is screen slack too. In metres the same handle would be easy to grab
zoomed in and impossible zoomed out.

Two decisions inside it are about failing loudly. A non-finite point degenerates
the box at ZERO rather than spreading `NaN`, because a `NaN` corner makes MapLibre
answer an empty list in silence — indistinguishable from "no handle there" —
while a box at zero also finds nothing and at least reads as a number when
debugging. And a negative or non-numeric tolerance degenerates instead of
inverting the box, since an inverted box is accepted and answers unpredictably.

THE CENSUS IS THE HALF THAT LASTS. The maths is pure and tested with its edges,
but what keeps the sixteen sites honest is a structural sweep over `git ls-files`
that fails on any query naming a handle layer without going through the box. It
named all sixteen before the fix, which is how the list was built; a thirteenth
tool written next year fails it until it complies.

Verified: frontend suite 750 files and 13758 tests, exit 0.

fix(touch): stop the pinch from drawing, and let a finger delete a vertex

THE PINCH DREW ON TOP OF THE MAP. The brush ignores the second finger
(`isPrimary`), but MapLibre's `touchZoomRotate` does not: landing a second finger
mid-stroke zoomed the map UNDER the stroke, and what the person got was an
unwanted mark across the drawing. `map_sig.js` leaves that gesture on for
navigation on purpose, so the tool is what turns it off, for the length of the
stroke — beside the `dragPan.disable()` that was already there and was only half
the job.

A VERTEX COULD NOT BE DELETED WITH A FINGER in arrow, boundary and coordination
line. Their only path was the right click, and line, polygon and the trajectory
editor already carried the long-press twin. Three tools were left behind because
`setupEditRightClickListener` on its own looked like enough.

IT WIRES THROUGH `createLongPressHandler`, NOT `setupVertexRemoveLongPress` — the
helper line and polygon use — and the difference is design, not taste. That
helper runs the handle query ITSELF and hands over a finished handle, while
`handleEditRightClick` in these three runs its own query from `offsetX`/`offsetY`
and further tells apart the branch of a merged feature. Going through the helper
would mean duplicating here the rule for which handle is removable, and two
copies of that rule drift. This way the long press enters through the SAME door
as the right click and nothing is reimplemented.

Both of those went in wrong first and lint said nothing, which is the part worth
keeping: the helper takes `(map, options)` and I called it with three positional
arguments, and I built a `{ features: [...] }` payload for a handler that reads
`offsetX`. Undefined arguments and ignored properties are not syntax errors. What
caught it was reading the helper's signature and the handler's body.

The test double gained `touchZoomRotate`. A fake map has to carry the surface the
tool touches, or the case dies of TypeError and not of a product defect.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
test(tablet): run the UI layer under a real touch screen, and fix what it caught

THE ONLY LAYER THAT EXERCISES THE UI RAN DESKTOP-ONLY. A desktop context does not
match `(pointer: coarse)`, does not fire `touchstart` and does not accept
`locator.tap()`, so every touch defect could only be ASSERTED by reading code —
which is how this session found that a line or polygon vertex could not be
dragged with a finger, that a measurement could not be closed, and that the
two-finger menu was born off screen.

`playwright.tablet.config.js` spreads the base config and swaps `projects` for
one context with `hasTouch: true` and an iPad landscape viewport, which lands
inside the band of `utilities/tablet-mode.js` — above the phone cut, and so on
the desktop layout driven by touch, which is exactly the combination the product
ships and nobody measured. `isMobile` stays out on purpose: it also turns on the
Chromium meta viewport and rescales the page, and what is under measurement is
the product on a tablet, not the product resized by an emulator. `retries: 0`,
because a touch case that passes on the second try is the very thing not to
learn.

THE FIRST CASE IS THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN CONTROL: it asserts the context really
matches coarse pointer and the tablet band. Without it, a config missing
`hasTouch` would leave the other cases green while driving the desktop path.

AND THE FIRST RUN CAUGHT A DEFECT I HAD DECLARED FIXED. The panel push used
`padding-left`, and `Element.clientWidth` INCLUDES padding — that is the measure
MapLibre sizes its canvas from. The map kept its full width and was merely
shifted inside its own box, and `map.resize()` collected the same number as
before. It survived review, the whole suite, and a commit message of mine
stating that the mechanism worked. The push now shrinks the border box (margin
plus width), and the case measures the canvas losing more than 200px when the
panel opens.

Then the spec itself went red for the right reason: after the mechanism changed
it was still reading `paddingLeft`.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE, and the list matters as much as the rest: it is
Chromium with touch, not an iPad. Nothing here says whether Safari synthesises
`dblclick` from a double tap, whether a long press becomes `contextmenu`, whether
`requestPointerLock` exists, or whether a nine-millimetre finger hits a sixteen
pixel target — `tap()` always hits the geometric centre. Performance and memory
are the host machine's, not the device's.

Verified: three of three green under the tablet config, exit 0.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
test(touch): pin the two-finger menu to where the finger actually tapped

The guard for a fix that reached the branch inside another session's commit
(543c9e37) without a line of its message explaining it — we share one working
tree, and a path list drawn from `git status` picks up whatever the other session
just wrote. This file is the half that makes the fix provable.

WHAT IT PINS, and it pins BOTH ends on purpose. The two-finger tap builds a
synthetic event to reuse the shift-click path, and that object carried only
`shiftKey`; the consumer positions with `Math.min(e.originalEvent.clientX, …)`,
and `Math.min(undefined, n)` is `NaN`. A `left: "NaNpx"` declaration is invalid
and the browser drops it in silence, and since `.feature-selection-menu` is
`position: fixed` with no `top`/`left` in the sheet, the box sat at its static
position — after a `#map-sig` that fills the viewport height, which is to say
below the fold. The menu was built, filled, appended to the body, and invisible.

Fixing only the origin would let the next caller of that method repeat the hole;
fixing only the fallback would hide the origin behind a plausible position. And
the fallback tests `Number.isFinite` rather than `??`, because `NaN` passes
through `??` intact and would rebuild the same invalid declaration.

The position comes from the MIDPOINT and not from the canvas-relative point, a
distinction that only started to matter today: `point` subtracts the canvas rect,
and the canvas stops starting at zero on a tablet now that the panel pushes the
map.

Structural, because the suite runs on node with no DOM: there is no way to build
the element and read a computed style, so what is pinned is the shape of the two
places the fix touched. Negative control run both ways — reverting the stamp
turns two of the five cases red, restoring it turns them green.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
fix(touch): drag a line or polygon vertex with a finger, and declare the second axis

THE HANDLES SHOWED AND DID NOT OBEY. Line and polygon were the last two tools to
drag an edit handle through mouse events; the other nine (circle, ellipse,
rectangle, sector, text, arrow, boundary, occupied front, coordination) already
used pointer events with capture. MapLibre registers real DOM `mousedown` /
`mousemove` / `mouseup` listeners and synthesises nothing from touch, and the
browser would only emit the compatibility events for a tap that does NOT become
a drag — but the canvas container declares `touch-action: none` and MapLibre
calls preventDefault on `touchmove`, so the drag eats the gesture and no
intermediate `mousemove` is ever born. On a tablet the two most used drawing
tools could not move a vertex at all.

Three things came with the event swap, each one a touch requirement the circle
already had: pointer capture, so the drag survives the finger leaving the handle;
a primary-pointer guard, so the second finger of a pinch does not start a second
drag of the same handle from the wrong position; and `pointercancel`, without
which a system gesture ends the drag with no `pointerup`, leaving the flag stuck
true and the move listener leaking on the container.

The guards were right to go red, and the harness was already waiting: the fake
canvas had `setPointerCapture` and `getBoundingClientRect`, and one of the two
files already carried a pointer burst written for the nine tools that were
already this way. What was missing was aiming at it. Nine call sites moved from
map-event shape to a `ptr(x, y)` helper; the fake canvas sits at (0,0) and the
fake `unproject` is the identity, so the coordinates that reach the tool are the
same ones that were written by hand before.

AND THE CENSUS ENTRY THAT D1E4D3A6 OWED. `listCatalog` gained a second query
when the catalog tab was scoped by production, so the surface census counted four
contact lines where two were declared. It is declared as four now, with both axes
written out: ACCESS is the default and fails closed, PRODUCTION enters only with
`producedOnly` and carries the inverse risk — it does not leak, it HIDES, since a
caller with no principal produces nothing and the institutional collection
(`owner_org_id` null) falls outside an equality comparison.

That failure was in my own backend run and I reported three failing files instead
of four: I had piped the log through `head -20` and read the window as the whole
list. A peer session in this same tree found it and asked whose it was.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
feat(tablet): give tablets a band of their own, and let the panel push the map

No tablet ever reached the phone layout. The cut is 480px wide (or 440 tall with
a coarse pointer, for the phone on its side), and an iPad is 768, 820 or 1024
points in both directions: every tablet, in every orientation, landed on the
desktop layout — the one that assumes a mouse, a hover and a right click —
driven by a nine-millimetre finger.

THE BAND IS THE COMPLEMENT, which is what keeps it honest: a tablet is a coarse
pointer that is not a phone. Writing a width of its own here would mint a third
number for someone to forget; derived from the phone cut, moving that cut moves
this one with it. `utilities/tablet-mode.js` is a leaf with zero imports, so a
page without a map can ask about the band without dragging the store in, and the
phone cut moved there so it lives in one place.

THE PANEL NOW PUSHES. The sidebar overlays a map that never recedes, which on a
desktop costs nothing and on a tablet was measured: 56px of rail plus 400px of
panel over a 768 portrait window leave 312px of visible map, narrower than a
phone on its side — and since nothing re-frames the camera, the feature just
selected sits behind the panel in almost every case. The person edits the
attributes of something they cannot see.

The push is `padding-left` on the container rather than an `easeTo` with camera
padding. Both stop the feature from hiding; only the first stops the zoom
control, the scale, the attribution and half the drawing from living on a strip
the finger cannot reach. The offset comes from the `contentLeftOffset` the layout
event already carried, never from a second copy of the panel widths.

The CSS mirror uses range notation because stylelint demands it while the module
uses `min-width`, which every browser understands — range syntax only reached
Safari in 16.4, and a `matchMedia` that fails to match would switch the band off
in silence on an older iPad. The values are the mirror; the syntax is not.

GUARDS THIS COST, and every one of them was right to fail. The audit schema grew
a tenth field while the inventory said nine. The envelope reader lost one of its
two sites when the OM filter went. The filter bar lost its text control, so the
count of control types is two. The scope note for the administrator is gone, so
the test now asserts its absence and that the branch returning null still exists.
A spec cited a testid that no longer exists — the absence is now asserted through
the class, because the guard cannot tell an absence assertion from a broken aim.
The map's module ceiling went 726 -> 728, measured by control: commenting the
`tablet-panel-push` edge gives 727, commenting `tablet-mode` as well gives 726.

And one found by the suite that I had written about without chasing: adding the
access predicate to the shared filter block made it the eighth parameter, pushing
limit and offset to ninth and tenth. An integration test builds the `EXPLAIN` of
`LIST_AUDIT` with the parameter list written by hand and was handing nine where
the statement asks for ten. It passes `true` there, not `false`, because what
that case measures is the `target_id` index path: with `false` the plan would
gain the action `NOT IN`, which that index does not serve, and the measurement
would be about something else.

Verified: root lint clean on both packages; frontend suite green; backend suite
green except two files another session is editing in this same tree; e2e contract
leg green, 67 files and 251 tests against the real backend — which is where the
audit case written blind earlier today finally ran.

feat(admin): scope the catalog to the producer's OM, hide sign-ins from the trail

Three changes to the admin panel, plus the layout fix they exposed.

CATALOG, scoped by PRODUCTION. `GET /api/v1/<table>?producedOnly=true` swaps the
ACCESS axis (who sees it) for the PRODUCTION axis (who maintains it), reusing
`fn_can_produce_resource` in the WHERE — the same clause the 360 admin listing
already used, so the five sub-tabs now share one regime instead of two rules
wearing the same face. The flag is explicit and off by default: without it the
route still answers with the public collection plus whatever the caller reaches,
which is the contract the grant and loan cases measure.

The cut is STRICT, by the owner's call: the institutional collection
(`owner_org_id` null) goes with the other organizations', because the function
compares equality and null equals nothing. Today every seeded row is
institutional, so a producer whose organization has produced nothing opens on an
empty sub-tab. The tab's legend was rewritten to say so; an empty screen with no
explanation reads as a defect.

The same flag ships on every sub-tab, for the admin too: the function answers
true for that role, so his list is unchanged and the client carries no role `if`.

AUDIT, without sign-ins. Entries and exits (`LOGIN`, `LOGOUT` — exactly two;
refresh writes no trail and a failed login cannot be written, since `actor_id` is
NOT NULL) are hidden unless the new checkbox is ticked. The cut is server-side
because the tab paginates server-side and reads its `total`: filtering the page
in hand would make the footer claim "1 to 50 of 213" over a shorter list.
`COUNT_AUDIT` shares the same filter block, so the count follows the list.

The predicate has a third branch, and it is the one that avoids an empty screen:
an explicit action request WINS the cut. Picking "Entrada no sistema" in the
action select still works with the box unticked, because refusing in silence what
the screen itself offers is worse than the noise.

This broke a guard, and the guard was right to break:
`audit-trail.e2e.test.js` compared `soLogin.total` against the total of
"everything", and with the cut in place "everything" no longer counts logins.
Worse, the only row that base is guaranteed to hold is the LOGIN its `beforeAll`
plants, so an assertion of "at least one row" could fall to zero. Three calls now
ask for `includeAccess`; a new case pins the new behaviour.

ACCOUNT, a real form. The three sections were `<div class="...__form">`, and
Chrome said so four times on every open ("Password field is not contained in a
form"). Password managers navigate by the form, so a loose password field is
outside what the browser can offer and save, and the `current-password` plus
`new-password` pair stops reading as a password change. The button stays in its
own actions block and associates by `form="<id>"`, which also buys Enter-to-submit
— behaviour the tab never had. Both password forms carry a visually hidden
username field, without which the browser knows there is a credential but not
whose it is.

LAYOUT. The content column had a 1080px ceiling and no automatic margin, so it
hugged the left edge and left the whole gap on the right; on a wide monitor that
reads as a crooked page. And no prose in the file had a reading measure: the only
`ch` on a text element was the catalog legend. At 1080px a paragraph runs about
150 characters per line, twice the typographic norm, which is why the panel reads
as "too much text" even where no word is spare. Nine prose classes now cap at
70ch; tables, cards and forms keep their own width.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
retrospectiva 2026-09-19: o 1 CGEO ganha ferramenta de tarjamento, e a faixa so pelo teto aceita o degenerado

Duas paginas de wiki novas. tarjamento-documento traz o conceito de dominio: por que
tarja desenhada por cima nao remove o dado do PDF, quais sao as quatro portas do arquivo
(texto, anotacao, formulario, metadado), quais tres formas de conteudo so se leem por OCR
(pagina escaneada, texto em curvas, fonte sem ToUnicode), e o que os orgaos usam hoje.
tarja-1cgeo descreve a ferramenta propria, a banca de 41 itens e os limites conhecidos.

O achado da busca externa, que a resposta anterior nao tinha: a CGU mantem ferramenta de
tarjamento DENTRO do Fala.BR, a mesma plataforma por onde a DGEO responde LAI, e o manual
v1.2 dela declara que NAO trata imagem nem assinatura escaneada. O processo de aquisicao
64490.001122/2026-79 tem 3 de 21 paginas escaneadas, e cai exatamente nesse buraco.

MEMORY: a linha do rosto no 360 e a do tarjamento fundiram numa so, "dado pessoal nao se
publica sem tratamento". A memoria fica em 4.971 caracteres, 82,8%, ACIMA do gatilho de
consolidacao: proximo passo e mover detalhe duravel para a wiki, e a poda e do chefe.

DECISIONS ganha a entrada da ferramenta (contexto, alternativas recusadas, AGPL imposta
pelo PyMuPDF, raio de explosao e o que ficou aberto). A skill entregar-lai ganha o
roteamento: o tarjamento roda ANTES dela, porque o que sobe ao repositorio da DSG ganha
link publico e aberto.

Sete eventos no livro-razao, e duas classes que valem alem desta sessao:
  - faixa declarada so pelo TETO aceita o degenerado do piso. O filtro de glifo aceitava
    area <= 900, e linha de tabela tem area ZERO: as 423 linhas da DANFE viraram glifo e
    derrubaram a etapa de marcar. A constituicao ja manda exercitar todos os eixos da
    regua; falta dizer que o limiar fecha os DOIS extremos.
  - no Windows, dois nomes que diferem so por maiusculas sao o mesmo nome, e o erro nao
    da mensagem: o build terminou com sucesso e o pacote saiu com um arquivo a menos,
    duas vezes seguidas. Conserto generico: contar o que foi ESCRITO ao fim do build.

E a correcao do chefe sobre acento: README, docstring e texto de tela sao prosa, e a
constituicao so dispensa acento dentro de codigo, URL, caminho e identificador. Escrevi
tudo sem acento por habito de console, e foram 60 trocas de interface mais 52 blocos de
docstring para consertar.

commits.author: Maj Borba
commits.message:
feat: pytorch-smt-tools correction commands support \${paths.xxx} via sibling paths.yaml

build-sam-corrected-masks / build-slico-corrected-masks loaded their yaml
config with plain yaml.safe_load — no OmegaConf interpolation, no file
composition, unlike the Hydra-driven pytorch-smt CLI. That made it
impossible for those two configs to reference a shared external
base-paths file the way every other config in an experiment set can.

_load_config_with_paths loads via OmegaConf instead and auto-merges a
sibling paths.yaml (same directory as the command's own yaml_path) before
resolving interpolations — the non-Hydra equivalent of Hydra's
`defaults: - paths`. Backward compatible: no sibling paths.yaml present
(the common case today) behaves exactly as before.

commits.author: Maj Borba
commits.message:
feat: GPU-accelerated O2C via cuCIM, auto-detected with exact CPU fallback

online_object_correction's connected-component labelling ran per-image,
every batch, CPU-only (.cpu().numpy() + skimage/scipy) — a real hot path
in correct_base=iter mode. Evaluated kornia.contrib.connected_components
first and rejected it: verified against skimage on realistic 256x256
masks, it mismatched in 41/60 trials at its default num_iterations=100,
and needed ~512 iterations (5x default) to reach 0/60 in that sample with
no formal convergence guarantee — not acceptable for an operation that
decides which pixels a published method corrects.

Switched to cuCIM (RAPIDS) instead: connected-component labelling has an
exact solution, so cuCIM's output is identical to skimage's by
construction, not empirically approximated. Single implementation
parameterized by xp/ndi/label_fn (numpy+scipy+skimage vs cupy+cuCIM) so
the CPU path is untouched and still exactly what's tested. GPU path
auto-selected via use_gpu=None when the input tensor is already CUDA and
cuCIM is importable; DLPack zero-copy, no host transfer. use_gpu=True
forces it (raises clearly if cuCIM missing); use_gpu=False forces CPU
regardless of device.

pyproject.toml already had a gpu-ml extra pinning cucim-cu12/cupy-cuda12x
to the CUDA 12.x line, which happens to be exactly what a Tesla V100
needs (compute capability 7.0, and torch's default wheel moved to CUDA 13
which dropped Volta support) — documented that connection in the README's
new "AIO2 O2C GPU Acceleration" section.

Not exercised by this dev machine (no CUDA) beyond the dispatch-decision
logic — TestGpuCpuEquivalence in test_o2c_correction.py is the actual
correctness check, skipped here, runs on any CUDA host.

QUATRO PEDIDOS DO DONO (2026-09-18), tres deles defeitos que so o uso mostrou. O que os une e o
mesmo assunto: a lista de comentarios atravessa superficies, entao "ir para" tem de LEVAR.

1) FECHAR O QUE ESTA ABERTO. "Se tiver com 3d aberto ou 360 e clicar num comentario do maplibre na

   NAO e o destino, antes de ir. A conta e por SUPERFICIE e nao por comentario: ir de uma foto para
   outra nao fecha o 360, senao a tela piscaria a toa.

2) EDITAR O COMENTARIO. Cada entrada (raiz ou resposta) ganhou "Editar" para quem pode modifica-la,
   com o mesmo gate de resolver e excluir, que o servidor aplica pela coluna `author_id`. O editor
   nasce com o texto atual e com o salvar ja liberado, porque editar e quase sempre corrigir: caixa
   vazia obrigaria a reescrever tudo, e botao desabilitado obrigaria a mexer no texto antes de
   poder salvar. Grava por `updateComment`, no cartao comum, entao as tres superficies ganham junto.

3) A FOTO ERRADA. "Ao no mapa principal clicar num comentario do 360 ele abre na foto errada."
   A camada de comentarios do 360 e montada na ABERTURA do visualizador, e andar pela seta troca a
   foto por `loadPhoto`, que nao passa por la. A camada ficava com a foto da abertura: desenhava os
   baloes da foto ERRADA e, pior, GRAVAVA o comentario novo com ela -- e ai o painel abria noutra
   foto mais tarde. Ela passa a assinar `STREETVIEW_360_PHOTO_CHANGED`, trocar o escopo e fechar o
   cartao que ficou para tras.

4) O 3D NAO ABRIA. "Ao no mapa principal clicar num comentario do 3d o 3d nao abre." O painel
   chamava `openViewerWithTileset`, que MONTA a cena do Cesium e mais nada; quem esconde o mapa 2D e
   mostra o container do 3D e `setFullMap(false)`, dentro do `openViewer` do CONTROLE. A cena

UM QUINTO DEFEITO, QUE A PROVA ACHOU e nao estava no pedido: o cartao da superficie anterior ficava

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
dev: o terreno do 3D tambem sai do ambiente autossuficiente

MEDIDO EM 2026-09-18, tentando abrir um modelo 3D nesta estacao: o visualizador ficava em
"Carregando cena..." para sempre, com o container em `display: none` e o canvas em 0x0. A causa nao
era o modelo: era o TERRENO. O Cesium busca o `layer.json` do provider de terreno e, sem resposta,
a cena nunca fica pronta -- a unica pista era um `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` no console, sem nada na
tela dizendo o que faltava.

O terreno do 3D e um SERVICO A PARTE do terreno do 2D (`MAP3D_TERRAIN_URL` contra `TERRAIN_URL`), e
so a producao o serve. O ambiente que o dono pediu em 2026-09-17 -- "para nao depender de pegar
coisas do servidor de producao do ebgeo" -- ja desligava grid, sombreamento e terreno do 2D, e
deixava este de fora por nao ter sido exercitado ate hoje.

QUEM DESLIGA E O OVERRIDE, e nao a variavel de ambiente: `node --env-file` carrega o `.env` do
backend por cima do que se passa na linha de comando, entao `MAP3D_TERRAIN_URL=""` nao teve efeito
nenhum. O override de `config_settings.app_config` vence, que e o mesmo mecanismo que o resto desta
funcao ja usa, e `--restaurar` devolve o terreno junto com os outros tres.

Sem terreno o Cesium usa o elipsoide, que e o comportamento declarado de quem nao tem terreno no
proprio `config.service.js` ("So habilita quando ha URL configurada").

O QUE ISTO NAO RESOLVE, e fica dito: o `.3dtiles` precisa estar onde `MODELS_3D_DIR` aponta. Nesta
estacao os tres modelos do acervo (`serra_dourada`, `cmdo14bda`, `4rcb`) ja estao em disco, mas a
chave do `.env` aponta para uma pasta que nao existe aqui -- e ai o backend responde 404 no
`tileset.json` e o visualizador abre vazio. E ajuste de ambiente do operador, nao de codigo.

feat: idempotent ExperimentsRunner + parallel Pipeline runner with GPU-aware DAG scheduling

ExperimentsRunner: resume now defaults to true (idempotent re-launch by
default); new overwrite (bool | list[run_idx]) forces specific completed
runs to redo, cleaning stale output dirs first. Applies to both the
seed-only and k-fold loops.

New PipelineRunner (mode: run-pipeline): runs a DAG of independent
experiment steps — different models/losses/datasets, or non-Hydra CLI
commands (e.g. pytorch-smt-tools data-prep tools) — each as its own
subprocess. Steps declare depends_on for ordering (validated for unknown
refs/cycles) and gpus/vram_gb for scheduling: gpus=0 draws from a CPU
pool, gpus=1 bin-packs onto free VRAM, gpus>1 reserves whole GPUs
exclusively for distributed (DDP) steps, via CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES.
Idempotent by default (pipeline_state.json), same overwrite semantics as
ExperimentsRunner, on_error stop/continue, preflight config validation
pass, and per-step + master log files.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
comentarios: o 3D fecha o pedido, e o painel lista as tres superficies

Terceira e última etapa do pedido do dono (2026-09-17). O 3D ganha o mesmo sistema, e o painel de
comentários passa a listar as três superfícies com o caminho de volta para cada uma — que é a outra
metade da decisão dele: o comentário desenha só onde nasceu, e a lista é quem leva até ele.

O 3D é o gêmeo do 360, com a API da superfície dele: a âncora é o modelo mais o ponto sobre ele
(`lng`, `lat`, `alt`, o que `scene.pickPosition` devolve), o desenho é uma entidade do Cesium com um
billboard desenhado num canvas (a MESMA figura do pino do mapa e do balão do 360: a cor do autor com
as iniciais dentro e o contador de respostas), e o cartão é ancorado em pixel, pela mesma razão do
360. O cartão, os gates e as ações continuam vindo de `comment_tool/comment-card.js`.

NOMES IGUAIS AOS DO MAPA, e isso é escolha: o comentário 3D guarda `lng`/`lat`/`alt`, e não um par
de nomes próprio, porque o 3D é o mapa com uma altura a mais. Um vocabulário novo obrigaria o painel
a saber de qual superfície veio para ler a mesma coisa.

O CLIQUE NUM BALÃO EXISTENTE GANHA SEMPRE, mesmo com o modo de comentar ligado: clicar para
responder é mais frequente que criar outro exatamente em cima.

O PAINEL DESPACHA POR SUPERFÍCIE. Clicar numa linha leva ao comentário: no mapa voa até a
coordenada, no 360 abre a foto JÁ APONTADA para a direção dele (pelo `targetOrientation`, o mesmo
caminho que a aba de camadas usa para abrir uma foto virada para um marcador) e no 3D abre o modelo
e voa até o ponto. O despacho é por `surface`, nunca por adivinhar qual campo está preenchido — é
justamente adivinhar que faria um comentário 3D, que TEM `lng`/`lat`, ser tratado como do mapa. A
linha ganhou a etiqueta da superfície ("Mapa 1 · 360"), e o mapa continua sem etiqueta de propósito:
ele é o caso comum, e etiquetar todas as linhas só acrescentaria ruído.

VERIFICACAO. `npm run lint` rc=0 e `npm run test:frontend` verde depois da última escrita (712

comentarios: o 360 ganha o sistema inteiro, com o cartao do mapa

Segunda etapa do pedido do dono (2026-09-17): comentar DENTRO da foto 360, com as mesmas regras e
funcionalidades do mapa. A fundação (o campo `surface`, o cartão comum e a poda) veio no commit
anterior; aqui é a tela.

O QUE O USUÁRIO GANHA: um botão de comentar na barra do 360, o clique na cena escolhendo onde a
conversa fica, o balão com as INICIAIS do autor e o contador de respostas desenhado sobre o
panorama, e o cartão da conversa abrindo no clique — responder, resolver, reabrir e excluir, tudo
vindo de `comment_tool/comment-card.js`, o mesmo módulo que o mapa usa.

A ÂNCORA É A DO MARCADOR 360: foto, direção e inclinação. O balão é projetado pelo mesmo
`projectPOI` e entra no MESMO hit tester, o que lhe dá projeção, alcance de clique e reprojeção a
cada giro sem nada novo. Ele entra DEPOIS dos POIs de propósito: com um comentário exatamente sobre
um ponto, quem ganha o clique é o comentário, que é a coisa que tem conversa atrás dela.

O CARTÃO É ANCORADO EM PIXEL, e isso é decisão, não atalho: dentro da esfera não existe coordenada
onde pendurar um popup, e um cartão que perseguisse o balão andaria pela tela enquanto a pessoa lê e
escreve. Ele nasce onde o gesto aconteceu, é mantido dentro do container (perto da borda ele
escaparia da tela) e fica até ser fechado.

O BOTÃO SOBREVIVE AO SOMENTE LEITURA, e é a regra do produto: o Comentarista é o somente leitura
MAIS a função de comentar, então esconder o botão junto com os de edição tiraria dele a única coisa
que ele sabe fazer. A regra de CSS que esvazia a barra ganhou a exceção `#comment-360` ao lado de
`#help-360`, e quem decide se o botão aparece é `podeComentar()`, que pergunta por `CREATE_COMMENT`.

O DEFEITO QUE A MEDIÇÃO PEGOU, e que nenhuma suíte pegaria: o balão era projetado sem `distance`.
`sphericalToMeters` multiplica a distância pelos senos e cossenos da direção, então `undefined` vira
NaN nos três eixos; o marcador entrava no hit tester com `screenX` NaN e o resultado era não
desenhar e não ser clicável, SEM erro nenhum no console. A sonda que achou isso leu o hit tester por
dentro (`{"balao":[{"x":null,"y":null}]}`); depois do conserto, `{"x":551,"y":400}` e o hit test
responde `comment`. A constante agora tem o porquê escrito ao lado.

VERIFICACAO. `npm run lint` rc=0 e `npm run test:frontend` verde depois da última escrita (711
arquivos, 13.168 casos). Os censos da casa cobraram três coisas e as três foram atendidas: o tipo
`'comment'` do marcador entrou no censo de permissão como HOMÔNIMO (com motivo: é o que está
desenhado na esfera, não quem pode desenhar), o par (arquivo, campo) de `comments-360.js` entrou no
censo de referências, e o teto do grafo completo subiu de 708 para 709 arquivos, com o arquivo novo
nomeado e a razão de ele não entrar no grafo ANSIOSO.

E O ARRANQUE DO BACKEND COBROU A PEÇA QUE FALTAVA, que nenhum teste tinha pegado: o guarda estático
de `catalog.service.js` recusa subir quando uma superfície do registro não tem perna em
`COUNT_ATLAS_REFS_TO_RESOURCE`. A perna de `comments.modelo3d` foi escrita (conta os atlas vivos
que citam o modelo num comentário), e a prosa que enumerava as superfícies 360 sem perna passou de
três para quatro, nomeando `comments.foto360`.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
comentarios: a fundacao para 360 e 3D, com o cartao e as regras num lugar so

O PEDIDO DO DONO (2026-09-17): "da mesma forma que temos sistema de comentários no maplibre quero no
360 e no 3d, com as mesmas regras e funcionalidades". Decisão dele na mesma conversa: o comentário
desenha SÓ na superfície onde nasceu, e as três aparecem juntas no painel, que leva até elas.

Este commit é a FUNDAÇÃO, e não a tela: o modelo, o cartão comum, a poda e o gate do servidor. O
desenho no 360 e no 3D vem em seguida, sobre isto.

UMA ENTIDADE, E NÃO TRÊS. O comentário continua sendo `comment`, na coleção do MAPA, com o mesmo
documento lateral, o mesmo guarda de permissão e o mesmo sync. O que muda é `surface` mais a âncora
que aquela superfície usa, pelo padrão do MARCADOR de cada uma:

    '2d'  -> lng, lat                     (a coordenada do mapa)
    '360' -> photoName, heading, pitch    (a foto e a direção dentro dela)
    '3d'  -> tilesetId, lng, lat, alt     (o modelo e o ponto sobre ele)

O precedente é o cursor de presença, que ganhou `surface` em 2026-09-16 pela mesma razão. E os
campos ATRAVESSAM O SERVIDOR SEM MIGRAÇÃO, medido antes de escrever a linha: o payload de `comment`
está em `SCALAR_PAYLOAD_ENTITIES`, que preserva todo escalar; o INSERT grava `JSON.stringify(data)`
inteiro na coluna `data` JSONB; e o retrato devolve `...c.data`.

O CARTÃO VIROU MÓDULO (`comment_tool/comment-card.js`), com as regras dentro: os dois gates (quem
comenta, quem modifica ESTE comentário), responder, resolver, reabrir, excluir, o tempo relativo e a
autoria. "As mesmas regras e funcionalidades" só é verificável se for O MESMO código — três cópias
divergem no dia em que uma delas mudar. O que NÃO foi para lá é o pino e o posicionamento: o 2D
ancora por coordenada num popup do MapLibre, o 360 desenha no canvas do panorama e o 3D numa
entidade do Cesium, e não há nada em comum entre os três.

O OVERLAY DO 2D passa a montar esse cartão e a FILTRAR POR SUPERFÍCIE. O filtro não é decorativo: o
comentário do 3D tem `lng`/`lat` (o ponto sobre o modelo) e desenharia no mapa como se fosse dele.

A REFERÊNCIA NOVA EXIGE PODA, e esta é a parte que o pedido não menciona e o produto cobra. Um
comentário 360 guarda o NOME DA FOTO e um comentário 3D o id do MODELO: os dois são referência a
recurso de catálogo, que pode ser privado. Sem tratamento, um `.ebgeo` exportado levaria o id junto
e a tela do destinatário mostraria uma conversa sobre algo que ele não alcança.

  - duas superfícies novas nos DOIS registros (cliente e servidor), que o teste de espelho compara;
  - `podarDocumentoDeComentarios`, com uma regra própria: a CONVERSA CAI INTEIRA. A resposta não tem
    âncora, só `parentId`, então nenhuma varredura por id de recurso a alcançaria, e deixá-la seria
    guardar conversa sem o que ela comenta. É a mesma razão do `ON DELETE CASCADE` da tabela;
  - o GATE do sync no servidor: `resource-ref.extractors.js` ganhou o target `comment`, que lê as
    duas chaves. Sem ele, um comentário feito dentro de uma foto privada seria aceito de quem não
    alcança aquela foto. Isto é segurança, e não inventário.

VERIFICACAO. `npm run lint` rc=0 e `npm run test:frontend` verde depois da última escrita (711
arquivos, 13.168 casos); no backend, os censos de referência (`sync-referencia-de-recurso-censo`,
`classificacao-de-referencias`) passam. As réguas da casa cobraram quatro coisas nesta leva e as
quatro foram atendidas com dado, não com número novo: o orçamento de módulos ansiosos da pasta
(3 -> 4, com a razão escrita), o espelho dos dois registros, a fixture DOURADA da poda (que ganhou
comentários nas três superfícies, mais duas respostas) e o censo de pares (arquivo, campo). O caso
novo da resposta órfã reprova se a segunda passada do podador sair.

commits.message:
somente leitura: o seletor de mapa base e as barras do 360 e do 3D somem

O RELATO DO DONO (2026-09-17, testando um mapa somente leitura na rede local): "testei aqui um mapa
somente leitura e ele ainda está exibindo a escolha de basemap. Tambem quero que as ferramentas do
360 e 3d sejam suprimidas no modo de somente leitura do mapa".

AS QUATRO SUPERFÍCIES perguntavam SÓ pela trava do mapa (`isCurrentMapLockedSync`) e nada sabiam do
papel no atlas, que é exatamente a metade que o inventário de 2026-09-16 nomeou. Elas nasceram fora
daquele censo porque não desenham nada errado sobre um mapa travado: o defeito só aparece para quem
entra com compartilhamento `read` ou por link público.

  - O SELETOR DE MAPA BASE. Trocar de base é ESCRITA: `setBaseLayer` pede `GuardAction.UPDATE_MAP`,
    grava uma op `baseLayer` no documento do mapa e PROPAGA a troca aos outros usuários do atlas
    (foi o que esta mesma linha ganhou em 2026-09-16). O leitor via o cartão, clicava, e a escrita
    morria no guarda da store, que é o "desenha e recusa" que o dono mandou eliminar. A ação citada
    é a que o comando exerce, e não o padrão do módulo.
  - AS BARRAS DO 360 E DO 3D. A regra de CSS que faz o desenho já existia e já era a certa
    (`#toolbar-360.map-locked .button-tool-360:not(#help-360)` e
    `#toolbar-3d.map-locked .button-tool-3d:not(#help-3d, #voar-camera)`): o que faltava era a conta.
  - A ABA DE CAMADAS, pelo mesmo motivo e no mesmo gesto.

UM SEGUNDO DEFEITO NO MESMO LUGAR, achado ao consertar o primeiro: a barra do 360 aplicava o estado
APENAS no evento, e nada o aplicava na ABERTURA. Ela nascia inteira sobre um mapa travado e só se
corrigia se alguém destravasse e travasse de novo.

O ASSINANTE ÚNICO é o conserto da causa, e não só do sintoma. Cada superfície assinava
`MAP_LOCK_CHANGED` por conta própria, o que cobre metade: com o papel na conta, entrar, sair,
conectar e trocar de atlas mudam a resposta sem tocar em trava nenhuma.
`assinarEdicaoIndisponivel` (em `store/edicao-indisponivel.js`, onde a conta já morava) assina os
cinco eventos, chama o callback UMA VEZ na assinatura e devolve como desassinar. `MAP_LOCK_CHANGED`
cobre dois fatos de propósito: `setCurrentMap` o emite ao trocar o mapa ativo, e a trava é por mapa.

OS PORTÕES DE GESTO acompanharam o desenho: seis `isCurrentMapLockedSync` viraram `semEdicaoSync`
(no 360, marcador e as duas orientações; no 3D, a ativação de ferramenta e as duas da câmera). O
comando escondido ainda é alcançável por atalho de teclado, e o portão é o que fecha esse caminho.

A CLASSE CONTINUA `map-locked` nos dois CSS, pelo custo de trocá-la em dois arquivos e nos testes
que a leem. O que ela significa desde hoje é "não dá para editar agora", pelo motivo que for, e as
duas folhas dizem isso por escrito onde a regra mora.

VERIFICACAO. O censo de somente leitura ganhou as quatro superfícies e três blocos novos (o CSS das
duas barras, os seis portões de gesto e o assinante único): 26 casos, verdes.
`npm run lint` rc=0 e `npm run test:frontend` verde depois da última escrita (711 arquivos, 13.167
casos).

PROVA DE TELA, com dois navegadores contra o ambiente real em HTTPS, um atlas compartilhado como
`read` e o DONO como controle positivo em cada linha:

                          LEITOR                      DONO
  seletor de mapa base    ausente                     presente
  barra 360 (botões)      só `help-360`               add-marker, salvar-orientacao, share, help
  barra 3D (classe)       `map-locked`                sem classe

O QUE NAO FOI PROVADO NA TELA: a lista de botões visíveis do 3D. A barra não chegou a ficar visível
no ambiente headless para nenhum dos dois usuários (o Cesium não monta a cena ali, como já
registrado em 2026-09-16), então o que a sonda pôde discriminar foi a CLASSE, que é o que decide, e
o CSS que a consome está preso por teste.

commits.author: Maj Diniz
commits.message:
mapa: o botao do meio gira e inclina, sem tecla nenhuma

O PEDIDO DO DONO (2026-09-17): "no maplibre consigo configurar o botão do meio para inclinar e girar
o mapa? Hoje o botão direito é menu, e para inclinar ou girar é shift e ctrl, mas queria tb uma
versão sem shift e ctrl com o botão do meio".

A RESPOSTA DA PRIMEIRA PERGUNTA É NÃO, e foi medida na fonte instalada: na 6.9.1 o botão de cada
gesto do MapLibre é um literal dentro da fábrica do handler (a de rotação por mouse aceita o botão
esquerdo com Ctrl ou o botão direito, e nada mais), não há opção que o altere, e o gerenciador de
handlers só expõe a lista interna deles. O app não depende disso: ele declara `dragRotate: false`
em `createMap` e traz o gesto próprio desde 2026-09-01, então a decisão é de
`map/drag-rotate.model.js`.

O GESTO. `resolveDragMode` devolve `DRAG_MODE.BOTH` para o botão do meio, ANTES da recusa por
botão, e sem olhar modificador nenhum: o botão do meio é o gesto inteiro e responde igual com Ctrl,
Shift ou Meta apertados. Ele é o único botão livre no mapa, e é por isso que serve: o esquerdo
seleciona e arrasta, o direito abre o menu de contexto e encerra desenho em andamento. O
`preventDefault` que já existia no `mousedown` mata de graça o autoscroll do Windows, que sem ele
rolaria a página em vez de girar o mapa.

O QUE A MUDANÇA QUEBRAVA, e é a parte que o modelo não vê. `_onMouseUp` comparava o botão solto com
o ESQUERDO FIXO e ignorava os demais. Isso era certo, e continua sendo, para um clique com o direito
não encerrar um arrasto do esquerdo: encerrar ali reabilita o `dragPan` com o esquerdo ainda
apertado, e o MapLibre retoma a panorâmica do ponto velho do mousedown. Só que, com o botão do meio
arrastando, a mesma linha faz o `mouseup` DELE ser ignorado e o gesto nunca terminar: o mapa segue
girando com o botão solto, o `dragPan` fica desabilitado, e nada no console diz nada. O handler
passa a guardar o botão que começou, e só ele termina. Pelo mesmo motivo, a engolida do clique
sintético do fim do arrasto passa a ser de `auxclick` quando o gesto foi do meio, que é o evento que
esse botão dispara.

VERIFICACAO. Bloco novo em `frontend/tests/unit/drag-rotate-model.test.js` (o botão basta sozinho,
ignora todo modificador, e o '1' de um evento sintético mal montado não vale) e a suíte nova
`frontend/tests/unit/drag-rotate-botao-do-meio.test.js`, com onze casos sobre o HANDLER, `window` e
o container do mapa duplicados, e os dois controles que preservam a regra antiga.

CONTROLE NEGATIVO, executado em 2026-09-17: devolvendo `e.button !== 0` ao `_onMouseUp`, reprovam os
TRÊS casos do fim do gesto (a câmera continua andando com o botão solto, o `dragPan` não volta, e a
engolida é armada no evento errado) e os outros oito seguem verdes.

`npm run lint` rc=0 e `npm run test:frontend` verde depois da última escrita (711 arquivos, 13.156
casos). Nota de instrumento: numa rodada com o servidor de desenvolvimento no ar, três suítes de
linha de coordenação estouraram o `beforeAll` de 10 s que carrega o bundle do turf; rodadas isoladas
e a rodada com a máquina livre passam as três (154 casos).

PROVA VISUAL, contra o ambiente real e com o botão do meio de verdade: bearing de 0 para -60 e pitch
de 0 para 27 num arrasto só; soltando o botão, mover o ponteiro por mais 400 px não mexe a câmera; a
panorâmica com o esquerdo volta a funcionar logo depois; e o modal de atalhos mostra a linha nova.

retrospectiva 2026-09-17 (cont. 6 a 8): a prova tem de percorrer o caminho do usuario

Sessao de rede do DSGTools: as camadas do BDGEx nao carregavam no QGIS. O
defeito nao era do plugin nem do BDGEx, e o que eu embarquei primeiro nao
consertava o que o chefe via.

wiki/ti-infraestrutura ganha duas secoes medidas, e a primeira INVERTE o
reflexo que a pagina ja ensinava. Para servico interno o conserto e bypassar
o proxy; no QGIS o bypass e a causa. Com proxy no Windows e o proxy do QGIS
em branco, o QGIS nao alcanca nenhum host que o sistema manda contatar
direto: dez hosts medidos no 3.44.14 e no 4.2.1, as duas polaridades, e so o
loopback escapa. O eixo nao e com proxy contra sem proxy, e decisao
explicita contra heranca, e as tres configuracoes coerentes funcionam. A
segunda secao mede o repositorio de confianca: o conjunto de CAs do QGIS E a
loja ROOT do Windows, 81 contra 81, enquanto o urllib carrega 150, a loja
mais o pacote dele. Isso derruba a premissa escrita no DSGTools em agosto, e
explica o dialogo de excecao SSL que uma estacao mostrou, cuja armadilha e
gravar excecao permanente por host.

conventions/contrato-de-pronto ganha tres regras e o caso que as produziu. A
prova percorre o CAMINHO do usuario, mesma thread inclusive, porque medir a
camada pela thread principal aprovou uma tela que ficava branca. Alavanca
que funciona com valor podre nao e a alavanca, porque a fabrica de proxy que
eu embarquei produzia o mesmo efeito devolvendo 127.0.0.1:9. E bancada que
reprova todos os cenarios ainda pode estar certa: declarei a minha quebrada
e o QGIS Desktop do chefe reproduziu a saida dela erro por erro.

livro-razao: tres eventos, verificacao-vazia, afirmado-sem-medir e

Memoria do harness: duas paginas novas, o defeito de proxy do QGIS e a

fix(bdgex): troca contorno inutil por aviso, e corrige premissa medida errada

O contorno anterior (insertProxyFactory) nao resolvia o problema do usuario.
Ele fazia o dataProvider().block() passar na thread principal e me deu um
"camada valida" enganoso, mas a tela renderiza em outra thread e continuava
em branco, sem erro nenhum. Medido: 512x512 com uma unica cor e job.errors()
vazio. Pior, o efeito vinha de INSERIR a fabrica e nao do que ela devolvia,
porque queryProxy nunca era chamada e uma fabrica devolvendo proxy podre
funcionava igual. Sai inteiro.

O defeito e maior do que o BDGEx. Em maquina com proxy no sistema e o proxy
do QGIS em branco, o QGIS nao alcanca NENHUM host que o sistema manda
contatar diretamente: medido com QTcpSocket cru, sete hosts nessa condicao
falham todos com "The proxy type is invalid for this operation" e nem abrem
o socket, enquanto os dois que devem passar pelo proxy chegam la e so falham
em autenticacao. So o loopback escapa. Uma hipotese intermediaria minha, de
que a quebra vinha da excecao casar por nome e nao por IP, foi REPROVADA
pelo caso degenerado: quatro hosts internos onde nome e IP concordam falham
igual.

Fica o que tem conserto no plugin: o retry do GetCapabilities com gerente de
rede proprio, que monta o menu, e um aviso honesto dizendo que a camada nao
vai desenhar enquanto o proxy nao for decidido em Configuracoes, Opcoes,
Rede. Servem as duas formas, rotear o BDGEx pelo proxy ou preencher o proxy
e excluir o host do BDGEx para ele ir direto; as duas foram medidas
desenhando, com WFS em 5.572 feicoes. O aviso vai para o log sempre e para a
barra uma vez por sessao, dentro de try/except porque ele mora no caminho de
SUCESSO e o iface nao existe no qgis_process nem no dsgtools_cli.

Corrige tambem a premissa escrita em 90f3bd48 e no CHANGELOG, que a medida
derrubou: o urllib NAO ignora o repositorio de confianca do sistema. Ele
carrega 150 raizes contra 77 do Qt, a loja ROOT do Windows inclusa, e a raiz
local do Kaspersky aparece nas duas. O conjunto do Qt e exatamente a loja
ROOT, 81 certificados e nenhum fora dela.

fix(bdgex): contorna proxy nao resolvido pela pilha de rede do QGIS

Em maquina com proxy configurado no sistema e os hosts do Exercito na lista
de excecao (ProxyOverride com *.eb.mil.br no Windows), nenhuma camada do
BDGEx carrega. Medido no QGIS 4.2.1: um QTcpSocket cru, conectando por nome
a bdgex.eb.mil.br:443, falha com "The proxy type is invalid for this
operation" e nem abre o socket; o mesmo socket com setProxy(NoProxy)
conecta; e conectando pelo IP o erro vira "Authentication required", porque
a lista de excecao casa por NOME e nao por IP. A string vem da tabela de
erros do QNativeSocketEngine, dentro do Qt6Network. Fora do QGIS a rota
esta boa: os sete endpoints do BDGEx respondem 200, com TLS 1.3 e cadeia
valida ate a GlobalSign R46.

Nao e defeito do plugin nem do BDGEx: na mesma maquina plugins.qgis.org e o
tile da OSM tambem falham, e um QNetworkAccessManager puro, no mesmo
processo, baixa o GetCapabilities inteiro (41.563 bytes).

O GetCapabilities passa a ser refeito com gerente de rede proprio e proxy
resolvido a mao, e so quando o caminho normal ja falhou. Se o retry passar
onde o QGIS falhou, a maquina esta provada defeituosa e ai instala-se a
fabrica de proxy que destrava o provedor WMS, removida no unload. Maquina
sadia nao chega no retry e nao e tocada, o que vale tambem para macOS, onde
o defeito nao foi medido.

Ressalva registrada no proprio modulo: a fabrica conserta a camada WMS (4
de 4 falhas sem ela, 2 de 2 sucessos com ela, cache limpo a cada rodada),
mas queryProxy nunca e chamada e uma fabrica que devolve proxy errado
funciona igual, entao o efeito vem de inserir e nao do conteudo. Por isso
ela so entra depois da falha comprovada.

Junto: as URLs dos tres servicos passam a https, para onde o BDGEx
redireciona de qualquer forma (302 em todo endpoint), o que poupa um ida e
volta por tile; e o ramo que detecta resposta HTML em vez de XML, ate agora
mudo, passa a logar o inicio da resposta.
